articles.title: 1 Hot Take for Every Team After 2026 NBA Offseason
articles.summary: The 2026 NBA offseason is basically in the books, so we can now look at what all the trades, signings, draft picks, hirings and firings mean for the upcoming year.
articles.body:
The 2026 NBA offseason is basically in the books, so we can now look at what all the trades, signings, draft picks, hirings and firings mean for the upcoming year.

The Los Angeles Lakers made moves to strengthen the supporting cast around Luka Dončić. We've got strong feelings about how much of a difference those changes will make.

Meanwhile, the New York Knicks face a difficult road ahead after winning the 2026 title. Worn down, shedding talent in free agency and facing a tougher set of East opponents, the odds of our first repeat champ in a decade are looking long.

Let's prep for the year by handing out hot takes for every squad in the league.

Atlanta Hawks: A Blockbuster Trade Is Coming

There's a lot to like about how the Atlanta Hawks are constructed, led by 24-year-old All-NBA forward Jalen Johnson and his annual salary of just $30 million. Most Improved Player Nickeil Alexander-Walker is on arguably the most valuable mid-level contract in the league. Onyeka Okongwu is now a spacing, switchable center earning only $17 million per year.

All of those bargain starters are great, but none profile as first-option superstars. They're ideal support for exactly that kind of player, which the Hawks can get with $54 million in expiring salary between CJ McCollum, Lu Dort and Jock Landale.

The Hawks have a roster ready to accommodate an alpha with the resources to get one. It's pretty easy to see where this is headed.

Boston Celtics: Jaylen Brown Won't Be Missed...That Much

OK, sure, if the Boston Celtics find themselves deep in the playoffs, they're going to wish they had Jaylen Brown's ability to generate tough shots as a bailout option. There'll certainly be specific situations in which his one-on-one defense will also be missed.

Hasn't Boston earned the benefit of the doubt in a much broader sense? Why shouldn't we assume it knew what it was doing when it dealt Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers for Paul George and a pair of picks? Shouldn't we trust that the Celtics correctly judged the tradeoff between the positives and negatives (relative to his salary) that Brown provided?

We learned last year not to bet against a one-star Boston team led by maniacally competitive head coach Joe Mazzulla. With Jayson Tatum now taking Brown's place in that single-star setup, theoretically supercharging exactly the style Mazzulla wants to play, might the results be even better than they were a year ago?

Boston traded Brown mostly for long-term reasons, but the results this coming season will be far better than most expect.

Brooklyn Nets: Egor Dëmin Will Break Out

You can make a lot of mistakes by overvaluing Summer League play, but Egor Demin's growth was too obvious to ignore.

After shooting 38.5 percent from deep as a rookie and providing exactly the kind of connective passing the Brooklyn Nets hoped for when they picked him at No. 8, Demin flashed offensive dimensions in Vegas that could make him a dangerously complete weapon.

Demin averaged 21.0 points per game despite his three-point shot falling at only a 30.0 percent clip. He compensated for that with a new emphasis on attacking the basket, shooting 11-of-17 on two-pointers and getting to the foul line eight times. Last summer, he made only a single two-pointer and drew just one shooting foul.

Brooklyn targeted multiple guards in the first round last year. It looks like it found at least one true keeper in Demin.

Charlotte Hornets: No LaMelo, No Problem

The Charlotte Hornets decided they didn't want to be in the LaMelo Ball business. Everyone assumed the trade that sent him to the Minnesota Timberwolves was part of a deliberate retrenchment that would hurt the Hornets in the standings and delay the rest of the ascent that started last season.

This is a bet that Ball's departure was partly about financial prudence and capitalizing on his unusual health last year. It was also about the Hornets believing they could be better in the short term without him.

Coby White will provide most of what Ball did at a fraction of the cost, while Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller could thrive in larger on-ball roles. Perhaps Ball's absence will lead to better collective defense. It's not like the Hornets had any reason to believe he'd stay healthy going forward.

The bar here is last year's total of 44 wins. The Hornets can clear it without Ball.

Chicago Bulls: Caleb Wilson Will Explode

The seven threes Caleb Wilson hit in his Summer League debut got everyone talking. If the No. 4 pick could space the floor in addition to dominating the lane with his athleticism, it meant recalibrating expectations for both Wilson and the Chicago Bulls.

The 2026 draft class was loaded with top-flight talent in the lottery, but Wilson now appears to have as good a chance as anyone to win Rookie of the Year—an award he expects .

Wilson should have easier access to playing time than No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson and more quality talent around him than No. 3 selection Cam Boozer. Top choice AJ Dybantsa will have high-usage veteran stars soaking up scoring chances next to him in Washington.

Every report about Wilson's work ethic, drive and makeup has been glowing . Those should matter at least as much as the visual evidence that shows he has offensive dimensions most didn't expect.

Cleveland Cavaliers: Evan Mobley Needs to Take Over

We've trotted out some version of this take ever since the Cleveland Cavaliers landed Donovan Mitchell in 2022, but the fact remains that this team will go as far as Evan Mobley takes it.

Mitchell is a star, but he generally falls somewhere in the 6-10 range when ranking the league's best players in a given year. For Cleveland to improve on last year's Conference Finals run, Mobley must clearly surpass Mitchell in its hierarchy, marrying Defensive Player of the Year work on one end with at least All-Star-caliber offensive production.

Mobley regressed on offense last season, most notably by shooting 29.7 percent from deep after hitting 37.0 percent in 2024-25. He needs to reclaim the gains he made as a shooter, get back into the DPOY conversation and prove he can consistently create shots for others.

We wouldn't keep asking for so much if we didn't think Mobley was capable of delivering it.

Dallas Mavericks: Cooper Flagg Will Make the All-Star Team

Picks as highly touted as Cooper Flagg are supposed to be great in a hurry, but keep in mind that only six 20-year-olds have made the All-Star team this century.

Kyrie Irving will be back after missing all of last year while recovering from a torn ACL. While it might feel right to assume he'll provide playmaking that takes the pressure off Flagg, it's probably a mistake to bet on a 34-year-old coming off a major injury. Especially one who hasn't played more than 60 games since 2018-19.

Between the uncertainty surrounding Irving and Ryan Nembhard moving on, Flagg will find himself on the ball just as often as he was during his rookie season. That'll give him the opportunity to build on averages of 21.0 points and 4.5 assists per game. He'll also hopefully improve his 29.5 percent hit rate from deep and showcase the defense everyone was so excited about before the draft.

Denver Nuggets: Get Ready for a Bottom-5 Defense

Just about everyone who mattered on the Denver Nuggets' defense slipped last year. Aaron Gordon couldn't stay healthy, Nikola Jokić seemed to lose a step, Christian Braun didn't play up to his hefty extension and Jamal Murray's steal rate fell to a career low .

The one regularly disruptive force on the team, Peyton Watson, is gone via a sign-and-trade deal with the Cavs. DeMar DeRozan will replace him in the rotation; he is considered one of the worst defensive wings in the league.

The Nuggets might get more than 36 games from Gordon, but he's on the wrong side of 30 even if he stays relatively healthy. Even if he beats expectations and Braun returns to form, it's very difficult to see Denver improving on last year's No. 21 ranking in defensive efficiency.

There are several ways to arrive at the conclusion that Denver is done as a contender. The simplest one is to accept that this will be one of the five worst defenses in the league.

Detroit Pistons: They Didn't Solve Anything

Secondary creation was a major problem for the Detroit Pistons last season. It's hard to see how their offseason addressed the issue.

If you think shooting cures all ills, maybe you can see a solution in the additions of Isaiah Joe, Gary Harris and Taurean Prince. Perhaps John Collins will be a mild upgrade over the departed Tobias Harris—not overall, but specifically on the strength of his 40.6 percent conversion rate from distance last season with the LA Clippers.

Wouldn't it be more comforting if Detroit had found someone who could dribble and pass? Cade Cunningham carried an exceptionally heavy playmaking load last season. While Daniss Jenkins was a nice story, he wasn't up to the task of running the offense whenever the MVP candidate sat.

Unless Ausar Thompson takes a major leap or Jalen Duren adds even more offensive creation to his profile, the Pistons will face many of the same deficiencies that produced the worst postseason offensive rating of any team to play at least 14 games last spring.

Golden State Warriors: The Warriors Owe Steph Nothing

OK, obviously this take needs explaining because the Golden State Warriors would not have four championships since 2015 or be among the most valuable professional sports franchises in the world without Stephen Curry. He—not ownership, coaching or a great supporting cast over the years—is why the Dubs are what they are.

This gives rise to constant wailing about how the Warriors owe Curry. It's about them failing him by not shipping out every asset they have in a trade that still wouldn't turn the team into a contender.

What everyone seems to forget is that the two-time MVP has more agency than almost any star in the league. He's just fine with what the organization is doing.

If Steph felt he wasn't being treated with the appropriate respect, or if he believed the Warriors weren't properly balancing their present and future with his interests in mind, he could request a trade and upset absolutely nobody. Every executive, fan and teammate would completely understand and feel zero ill will.

If he's satisfied with what's happening in Golden State, what right does anyone else have to complain about it?

Houston Rockets: Steven Adams Matters Way Too Much

Steven Adams has a legitimate superpower. His offensive rebounding was critical to the Houston Rockets' offensive survival last season. This was evident from a plus-8.3 net rating boost during his time on the floor. That was the best figure on the team among players who logged at least 700 minutes.

Houston had more difficulty scoring when a healthy Adams was resting. Their offensive rating fell from 120.3 through Jan. 18 to 117.6 after he went down for the season with an ankle injury on that date.

The Rockets added veteran defender Marcus Smart and injury-prone guard Bogdan Bogdanović over the summer. Those two won't solve the team's half-court scoring issues on their own, which means Houston needs Kevin Durant to hold on, Reed Sheppard to explode and Amen Thompson to figure out how to shoot a basketball. If all that happens, maybe Adams won't quietly be the key to scoring success.

If it doesn't, a bruising 33-year-old backup big man will once again be too prominent in Houston's offensive fate.

Indiana Pacers: Tyrese Haliburton Will Have a Career Year

Part of this is an effort to speak Tyrese Haliburton's full recovery into existence. The NBA is better when singularly transformative offensive forces like him are healthy. The trickle-down effect is that the Indiana Pacers also get right back to serious contention in this hypothetical.

In addition to Haliburton entering his age-26 season at (hopefully) full speed, the Pacers' mid-year addition of Ivica Zubac could help create an even better version of the All-NBA point guard. Though he's mostly known for his interior heft and rebounding, Zubac is quietly a much more adept facilitator than Myles Turner, who was Indiana's starting center when Haliburton was last healthy.

The Pacers made the 2025 Finals on the strength of their dynamic offense. Zubac could add another dimension by working in concert with Haliburton. For this take to hold up, Hali would only need to make the All-NBA Second Team, which he's never done before.

LA Clippers: Darius Garland Is On the Block

The LA Clippers lost five of their own future first-rounders as a penalty for violating the salary cap circumvention rules, which increases the odds of trading for someone else's.

Two future firsts came back in the deal that sent Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors, which may lead to turning their attention to Darius Garland next. A two-time All-Star with two years and $87 million remaining on his current contract, Garland looked pretty close to his best self in limited action with LA last season.

He may not be an All-NBA superstar, but the 26-year-old is in his prime and probably ranks inside the top 10 at his position overall. Plenty of teams would happily give up a first-rounder or two for his services.

The Clippers are in for a long season either way, but they won't build anything sustainable without replenishing all the picks they lost.

Los Angeles Lakers: Expect a Top-5 Offense

The Los Angeles Lakers lost LeBron James, league-leading three-point marksman Luke Kennard, 67.1-percent shooter Deandre Ayton and Rui Hachimura's scorching outside sniping...and they're still going to finish with one of the league's five best offensive ratings.

That's a big deal because Los Angeles hasn't cracked the top five in scoring efficiency since way back in 2010-11 , when Kobe Bryant and Pau Gasol were coming off back-to-back titles.

Luka Dončić has his preferred roll man and offensive rebounder in Walker Kessler, as Austin Reaves proved last season he could be a first option when called upon. Add some improved shooting from new additions Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili. That can create the makings of a dominant attack.

Memphis Grizzlies: Cam Boozer Will Tie Magic Johnson

The rookie record for triple-doubles is 26, set by Oscar Robertson in 1960-61. Nobody's touching that, largely because defense was optional in that era and the pace of games was astronomically high.

The modern record belongs to Ben Simmons, who racked up 12 in 2017-18. Luka Dončić is third with eight, and all-time great Magic Johnson is fourth with seven.

That last figure feels about right for Cam Boozer, who was a double-double machine at Duke while averaging 4.1 assists per game. Great feel and court awareness are Boozer's defining traits. He will be surrounded by far better finishers in Memphis than he was in college. Assuming the Grizzlies give their prized rookie all he can eat in a key on-ball role, Boozer should be able to match Magic's seven triple-doubles en route to an easy All-Rookie nod.

Miami Heat: This is the League's High-Variance Champ

The presence of a hopefully healthy and potentially very motivated Giannis Antetokounmpo means the Miami Heat have to be taken seriously as a threat to win the whole thing. There may only be a half-dozen players with a serious chance to win MVP in 2026-27. Giannis must be counted among them.

Aside from concerns about how Miami strip-mined the roster to get Antetokounmpo, the potential issues with depth, shooting and health shouldn't derail them. If you have Giannis, the spectacular is possible.

Now, reframe your thinking. Give real weight to Antetokounmpo's injury issues last year. Acknowledge his age. Appreciate the scary level of dependence the Heat have on a 36-year-old Klay Thompson. Stress the odd fit between Giannis and Bam Adebayo. Question Davion Mitchell's fitness as a full-time starter. Bookmark Andrew Wiggins' iffy status as a stopper in what will be his 13th season.

Given all that, it's possible the Heat could miss the playoffs entirely.

No team has a bigger delta between its floor and ceiling than the Heat. It doesn't feel particularly close.

Milwaukee Bucks: Consensus Is Way Too Low

The Milwaukee Bucks have a pretty good chance to win more than the 32 games they did a year ago. This possibility isn't reflected in a projected win total in the mid-20s.

When you trade away a two-time MVP, expectations tend to dip. But the Bucks' loss is getting an outsized amount of shine compared to what they gained: multiple legitimate starters. That starts with Tyler Herro, who has been an All-Star, followed by a handful of rotation-worthy pieces.

Kel'el Ware, Kasparas Jakucionis and Jamie Jaquez Jr. are all capable of leveling up. They'll join quality players like Myles Turner, Ryan Rollins and AJ Green. Brayden Burries looks like a real find at No. 10 in the draft.

Toss in the fact that Milwaukee doesn't control its 2027 first-rounder and therefore has no reason to lose on purpose. You've got a team that could easily nudge up toward 40 wins with a good break or two.

Minnesota Timberwolves: LaMelo Ball's Career Hangs in the Balance

LaMelo Ball led the Charlotte Hornets to their best season in a decade. It wasn't enough to keep them from trading him.

That's the kind of thing that should make a player think.

Clearly, the Hornets didn't view Ball as someone they could trust in a major role going forward. Maybe extension-cost concerns had something to do with that, but durability, seriousness, defense and a broader worry about the type of team Charlotte wanted to be were all factors behind the move.

Now tasked with optimizing Anthony Edwards on a revamped Minnesota Timberwolves squad that views itself as a contender, Ball has everything to lose—or gain.

Stay healthy, drive winning, and prove the character-related and on-court warts are of the past. Ball can cement himself as a star in all the ways that matter. Missed time, staying lazy on defense or carrying over the maturity issues that marked his Charlotte tenure could leave Ball abandoned as a player worthy of a franchise's trust.

New Orleans Pelicans: Something, At Some Point, Will Happen

In the wake of an offseason where the New Orleans Pelicans' biggest move was retaining DeAndre Jordan, predicting the franchise will do anything transactionally certainly counts as bold.

Though the Pels have held off on moving Trey Murphy III, dangling Herb Jones or otherwise making an effort to retrench around Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen (an iffy proposition), their static status won't last forever.

When the season starts and the injuries New Orleans mostly avoided last year begin to crop up, it'll become clear to whoever is paying attention—which hopefully includes Joe Dumars and Troy Weaver—that there's nothing special brewing. At that point, trade talks should intensify as the overdue rebuild finally begins.

New York Knicks: This Is Not a Conference Finalist

Look, it's really hard to recover from a championship run. Everybody cites financial rules that create parity as the reason for nine different title winners over the last nine years. Sheer fatigue must be acknowledged as a major factor.

The New York Knicks thumbed their noses at win-probability statistics throughout the 2026 playoffs, stealing victories through some combination of grit, experience, sorcery and collective will. You could cite the sheer unlikelihood of repeating that feat to justify this hot take on its own.

But toss in a core that is mostly on the wrong side of 30, the loss of Mitchell Robinson, last year's exhausting march to the chip, improvements to multiple other East contenders on top of it, and you've got a recipe for a second-round exit.

Flags fly forever, but the Knicks won't be adding another this season.

Oklahoma City Thunder: Cason Wallace Won't Be Viewed As a Core Piece

There's long been a sense that Cason Wallace could do more. More self-created scoring, more pick-and-roll orchestration, more on-ball agency—surely the three-year vet would have flashed a wider array of skills if not for the stars ahead of him in the pecking order.

Wallace is a terrific defender against most guards and wings. He's been a serviceable three-point shooter on looks created for him by teammates. Those are valuable skills. But he has yet to showcase several others. It's getting harder to argue that the environment and surrounding talent in Oklahoma City are suppressing them.

Wallace's effective field-goal percentage has decreased over the last two years. He averages just 3.5 assists per 36 minutes while never getting to the foul line. Ajay Mitchell plays a different position, but he's a worthwhile comparison because his abilities to score and facilitate emerged immediately in the same circumstances that allegedly hid Wallace's.

Because Wallace probably doesn't have a set of untapped skills and is due for a hefty extension that the Thunder can't justify paying alongside all their other expenses, he's going to conclude the upcoming season outside OKC's long-term plans.

Orlando Magic: Orlando Will Have the Best Lineup in the NBA

We're making two bets here. The first is that the Orlando Magic's five best players will finally stay healthy enough to give this take some real weight. That feels much riskier than the second bet, which is that Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane, Franz Wagner, Paolo Banchero and Wendell Carter Jr. will dominate when they share the floor.

Last year, that group produced a net rating of plus-11.1 in 408 possessions—very good, but quite a bit short of the plus-15.0 territory to be in the running for the unofficial title of the league's best lineup in a given season.

Ideally, new head coach Sean Sweeney will coax better offense out of a group that is mostly young enough to improve. The possession total will increase to nearly 1,000.

Do that, hope for no ridiculous outliers like Charlotte's starting five putting up a plus-27.4 net rating last year, and Orlando's first unit has a real shot to grade out as the best of the best.

Philadelphia 76ers: VJ Edgecombe Will Be Philly's Second-Best Player

Joel Embiid will miss at least half the season, if history is any guide. LeBron James is closer to 50 than 30. Jaylen Brown, by some (specious) accounts, is no better than the Philadelphia 76ers' seventh-best player!

The path is clear for second-year guard VJ Edgecombe to produce more value than any Sixers teammate not named Tyrese Maxey.

Sure, a lot of this volume-based take rests on the assumption that Philly's pair of former MVPs won't hold up physically. The only area Edgecombe is likely to outproduce Brown is in the host of advanced metrics and on-off figures that have pretty much always disfavored the latter.

That still counts, and the four-way race for the honor of Philadelphia's second-most productive player will only get more interesting if the postseason promise Edgecombe showed turns into a full-on second-year leap.

Phoenix Suns: Khaman Maluach Will Be the Best Center on the Roster by December

Lottery picks are supposed to develop into starters, but Khaman Maluach's rookie season made a role of that size difficult to imagine. He barely played and appeared overwhelmed on the rare occasions the Phoenix Suns handed the big man any real playing time.

Summer League looked different. Maluach put up 19.5 points and 12.8 boards, drilling eight of 20 three-point attempts.

Do not expect a full smoothing of every rough edge. Maluach is going to keep making mistakes, occasionally looking lost and generally operating like most inexperienced 20-year-olds. That said, his production in Vegas felt like more than a blip.

Maluach looks and plays bigger than his listed 7'1" height. He has the potential to be physically overwhelming. That aligns nicely with his strong work ethic. Perhaps most importantly, he does that thing where he lets go of the rim after a dunk and ends up flat-footed.

Buy all the stock you can before the price goes up.

Portland Trail Blazers: Jrue Holiday Is Getting Traded

Portland Trail Blazers owner Tom Dundon embraces his well-deserved "cheapskate" label, but the team's roster has so far been spared from cost-cutting measures that have hit other parts of the organization.

That's going to change this year—partly because Dundon's recent history suggests there's no lower limit to his thrift, but also because the Blazers' glut of guards is too costly to justify.

Portland traded for Ja Morant, adding him to a positional group that already had Scoot Henderson, Shaedon Sharpe, Jrue Holiday and Damian Lillard. Don't forget that forward Deni Avdija has more right to on-ball reps than any of them. Sharpe is out with a torn meniscus. Lillard may be on a certain minutes restriction, but that's still too many guards.

Holiday is set to earn $34.8 million in his age-36 season. When the cost-cutting comes, that's where Dundon will start.

Sacramento Kings: A Terrible Contract Is Coming

The Sacramento Kings have just under $75 million in expiring money devoted to Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter this coming season. Chances are, they won't let those deals come off the books, intending to use cap space or take on unwanted contracts with picks attached.

More likely: Sacramento will chase a big name with one of the worst deals in the league, hoping for short-term relevance without a coherent long-term plan.

It's too early to guess exactly how the Kings will sabotage themselves, but we know owner Vivek Ranadive can't help himself based on the past. Keep an eye on Joel Embiid, Zion Williamson, Jalen Green, Anthony Davis (who they'd surely extend), Ja Morant and others.

If it's a bad deal attached to a starry name, it's on the Kings' radar.

San Antonio Spurs: Dylan Harper Will Win Sixth Man of the Year

Not hot enough? OK, how about this: Dylan Harper will win Sixth Man of the Year unanimously.

That's never happened before. It shouldn't happen this year because the Spurs should simply start their second-best player and worry about what that means for De'Aaron Fox later. But all signs point to Harper coming off the bench in the spirit of Manu Ginobili—who happens to have come closest in history to sweeping the Sixth Man vote.

He got 123 of the 124 first-place votes in 2007-08, with Leandro Barbosa snagging the lone outlier.

Fun facts: Ginobili finished 10th in MVP voting and made an All-NBA team that year. Harper is going to have a similarly dominant season and will remain a perennial Sixth Man favorite until the Spurs get their act together and start him.

Toronto Raptors: The Kawhi Leonard Trade Will Be a Disaster

Maybe it's just the stench of the freshly completed investigation into the Clippers' malfeasance, or perhaps it's driven by the feeling that karma is going to play a role in the massive move. Then again, the idea that things could go south with Kawhi Leonard doesn't have to rely on stuff like that.

We could point to one of the league's more storied injury histories and cite Leonard's age (35) to justify the creeping worry that the Toronto Raptors' biggest offseason move will not pay off.

Two unprotected first-rounders and a swap is no small price for a player who comes with considerable baggage and mileage. If the Raps get something close to the 65 games Leonard managed last year, while he produces at the same All-NBA level that leads to a deep playoff run, perhaps that'll be enough to justify the cost.

Having laid all that out, though, it's hard to imagine it coming to pass.

While losing Walker Kessler in a sign-and-trade hurts the Utah Jazz in the short term, the package they got from the Lakers was too good to ignore. We also need to acknowledge that his exit isn't the catastrophe oddsmakers seem to think it is.

The numbers are fluid, but Utah's over/under is currently falling somewhere in the mid-30s. That feels way too low in light of Keyonte George's leap, the addition of Jaren Jackson Jr. and another year of development for a youth corps led by Ace Bailey.

If George picks up where he left off, a non-load-managed Lauri Markkanen plays a full season and Jackson meets expectations, this team is going to smash that over. While the main offseason additions—Darryn Peterson, Jaxson Hayes and Josh Okogie—aren't likely to move the needle this year, the incumbent talent is enough to get Utah into the playoff picture.

Let's go with a tidy 44 wins, twice last year's total.

Washington Wizards: Alex Sarr Will Make 150 Threes

Alex Sarr shot 34.1 percent on catch-and-shoot triples last year. The presence of Trae Young means the quality and frequency of the third-year big man's open looks will increase.

Relatedly, Anthony Davis' window to prove he's a legitimate perimeter threat closed years ago. He'll do most of the screening and diving, which likely means Sarr spends more time outside the arc than he did last season.

As a rookie, Sarr hit 105 triples across 67 games. He lowered his volume last season while significantly improving his efficiency from 30.8 to 33.3 percent. Lest that make this take seem insufficiently hot, note that Lauri Markkanen is the only 7-footer to make at least 150 triples in a season since 2022-23.

Stats courtesy of NBA.com , Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass . Salary info via Spotrac .

Grant Hughes covers the NBA for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, where he appears with Bleacher Report's Dan Favale .

articles.title: Ex-Purdue star Trey Kaufman-Renn granted TRO to return to college basketball in latest eligibility ruling
articles.summary: Trey Kaufman-Renn was selected in the second round of the NBA Draft earlier this summer by the Timberwolves, but he never signed a contract with them.
articles.body:
Trey Kaufman-Renn may be able to play a sixth season of college basketball after all.

The former Purdue star was granted a temporary restraining order against the NCAA by a circuit court in Indiana's Clark County on Wednesday, according to the Indianapolis Star . He is just the latest player throughout college sports to receive a similar order in recent weeks and months.

Kaufman-Renn will have a hearing for a preliminary injunction in the future, which would serve as a long-term solution. He will likely need that in order to actually play college basketball this season, at Purdue or elsewhere. That hearing has not been scheduled. His move to return to college came after the NCAA's new five-in-five rule, which was announced in June — something Kaufman-Renn wasn't able to benefit from.

Kaufman-Renn played four seasons for Purdue after initially redshirting, and earned all-Big Ten honors during his junior campaign. He averaged 14.2 points and 8.3 rebounds last season with the Boilermakers, who he helped lead to the Elite Eight. Kaufman-Renn was a key piece on their team that reached the national championship game in 2024, too.

Kaufman-Renn then entered the NBA Draft this past summer, and he was selected in the second round by the Minnesota Timberwolves. He played for them in the NBA Summer League in Las Vegas. But Kaufman-Renn has not signed a professional contract with the Timberwolves yet, and likely wasn't on track to earn a spot in their active roster.

Even if Kaufman-Renn is granted his preliminary injunction, it's unclear where he would actually end up. All four power conferences have passed similar rulings recently banning players who participated in pro football from returning to the college level. Some of those leagues have included basketball in their initial policies, while others are expected to announce that in the future.

LSU has been at the center of the debate after attempting to add two players who signed NFL contracts, though the Tigers have since backed down. SEC schools are still expected to meet and discuss LSU and its future membership in the league.

Several players who either played in the G League or entered the NBA Draft attempted to return last year. Alabama's Charles Bediako was perhaps the most notable, but he only appeared in five games before his TRO was overruled . Baylor signed former NBA Draft pick James Nnaji in December, too, but he never played in an NBA game and instead was with FC Barcelona since 2020. Two other former G League players are set to play for programs next season, too.

It's unclear where Kaufman-Renn plays this season, or if he ends up getting to at all. But the first step on that quest has gone in his favor.

articles.title: Deni Avdija Projected To Leave Trail Blazers And Become Premium NBA Free Agent
articles.summary: Portland Trail Blazers called "sinking ship" as questions loom about Deni Avdija's future.
articles.body:
In today's NBA, teams have to be more careful than ever about who they spend their money on . With strict CBA rules and restrictions for teams that spend too much, many veteran players are caught in the middle as their own teams review their worth.

In Portland, this is the situation regarding Deni Avdija , who is coming off his first All-Star season with averages of 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.7 assists, 0.8 steals, and 0.6 blocks per game on 46.2% shooting from the field. As much as he has thrived with the Trail Blazers , they are not in a position to extend his contract after the conclusion of his current deal, which only has two years and $24 million left.

"The Blazers are kind of a sinking ship. They are not setting themselves up to preserve the cap space they're gonna need to renegotiate and extend Deni Avdija ," said insider Sam Quinn on the 'Third Apron' podcast . "Deni will make $11.875 million in 2027-28. The most he can get in a veteran extension is a 140% Year 1 raise, or $16.625 million. That's MLE money. He's not taking that. To pay him fairly, they'd need cap space to renegotiate and extend him."

The Trail Blazers have made strides of late, thanks to the heroic performances of Avdija, Scoot Henderson , Donovan Clingan , and young sharpshooter Shaedon Sharpe . On paper, they have a solid young core that will only get better on the floor, but critics remain doubtful of their current trajectory.

Besides the injury to Sharpe ( that will keep him out for months ), the Trail Blazers must also deal with the reality of their frugal owner, Tom Dundon, who has already made headlines for his cost-cutting methods . That's not to mention the logjam in the backcourt between guards Ja Morant , Damian Lillard , Jrue Holiday , and Scoot Henderson . By all accounts, the Trail Blazers are a team with glaring red flags, and Avdija clearly does not fit their timeline as a win-now veteran in his prime.

Rather than pay Deni to stick around and handicap their flexibility, the Trail Blazers are expected to let him go as they make space for their younger generation. Whether he leaves via trade or free agency in 2028, he will likely have to look elsewhere to secure the max-level deal he'll no doubt be seeking. The question is, where would the best fit be?

It's hard to predict what the situation will look like, but Avdija is the kind of player who can raise any team's ceiling. That's why we can expect multiple teams to express interest in a contract, including potentially the Clippers , Suns , and Rockets , who all have the incentive to strike a deal. There's also the Denver Nuggets , where Avdija could make a fitting replacement for Peyton Watson (at the right price).

For now, with two years left on his contract, the Trail Blazers are going to stick with who they have and see where they stand. Eventually, however, they will need to make a choice, and it could very well shake up the NBA hierarchy in a major way.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Reveals Coach K's Advice to WNBA Star Ahead Team USA's 2026 FIBA World Cup Run
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the United States women's team will take the court Thursday for the quarterfinals of the 2026 FIBA World Cup, and she studied the advice of a legendary coach to better prepare her for the moment.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the United States women's team will take the court Thursday for the quarterfinals of the 2026 FIBA World Cup, and she studied the advice of a legendary coach to better prepare her for the moment.

Doug Feinberg of the Associated Press reported Wednesday that Clark watched videos of former Team USA and Duke men's coach Mike Krzyzewski talking about assimilating to a star-studded national team roster with players such as LeBron James and Kobe Bryant.

The message that the only thing that matters is winning on this stage is what resonated with the Indiana Fever star.

"You have to set everything that you want to achieve personally aside," Clark said. "At the end of the day, people don't care about that if you have a gold medal hanging around your neck. So, that's my goal, and I think we have the group to do it."

The United States has won the last four editions of this tournament and last fell short in 2006 when it settled for the bronze. This year is once again gold-medal-or-bust with so many WNBA superstars leading the way, and that can be a motivating factor.

"You don't want to be the team that everybody talks about because you didn't win," Clark said. "You want to do what's expected and that's to win a gold medal. I think it would certainly help and hopefully it's just a step in the direction of where I want to keep building and hopefully the goals that I want to achieve of hopefully playing in the Olympics in '28."

The Americans have looked the part of gold-medal favorite thus far with a 3-0 record in group play, although they received quite a test from Italy.

While Clark and Co. handled China by 33 points and Czechia by 41 points, they trailed Italy in the fourth quarter before escaping with a 55-52 victory. Perhaps it was something of a wake-up call and an experience they can build on moving into the elimination rounds.

As for Clark, she wasted no time establishing herself with a double-double of 14 points and 11 assists in the opener against China. However, she had just one point and one assist against Italy before going 1-of-6 from deep on the way to nine points against Czechia.

Fortunately for her, she doesn't have to be the star every night on a team that includes Napheesa Collier, Breanna Stewart, Paige Bueckers, Angel Reese, Jackie Young and more.

"Obviously there's probably still a lot of pressure on me to perform at this level, but I think that's a great thing about USA basketball, it isn't like the WNBA," the Fever guard said. "You're probably not going to come out here and score 30 and have 10 assists. That's just not reality because of the talent we have."

That is exactly the message Coach K preached in the videos she watched.

articles.title: LSU President Wade Rousse ends Lane Kiffin’s SEC showdown, but there is still relationships to mend
articles.summary: A Birmingham Alabama federal court hearing was delayed after LSU backed down and finalized its roster without former pro-athletes Wright or Harris.
articles.body: The ongoing battle between the SEC and LSU was set to be heard in a courtroom on Wednesday afternoon in Birmingham, Alabama. But, just 10 minutes before the scheduled hearing in federal court over whether the SEC would be granted the power to enforce its rules pertaining to former pro-athletes returning to college athletics, lawyers for both sides met inside the chambers of the presiding judge to discuss a resolution. A decision was made to continue the case to a later date, if needed and cooler heads looked to prevail out of Baton Rouge. LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN Call it 'waving the white flag' or however you'd prefer, but LSU has backed down from its stance on adding players to their roster that have professional experience in some form or fashion. One night before the SEC was scheduled to ask a federal judge in Alabama for a temporary restraining order, LSU has finalized its roster for the upcoming season. That doesn’t mean the SEC is not going to be meeting on Thursday regarding potential punishments for the LSU Tigers, though. JUDGE GRANTS INJUNCTION AGAINST NCAA, SEC, ALLOWING ATHLETES WITH NFL TIES ELIGIBLE TO PLAY FOR LSU, OTHERS After nearly three weeks of court appearances involving multiple athletes in the Louisiana case, including former Ole Miss players Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, the Tigers decided not to add either player to its roster at any point this season. The decision comes after both sides were embroiled in a fight that saw SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey make an appearance in a Louisiana district court to testify on behalf of his conference. During those proceedings, the lawsuit filed by the SEC was brought up during questioning. INSIDE A LOUISIANA COURTROOM: SEC-LSU LEGAL CIRCUS PLAYED OUT LIKE A JOHN GRISHAM NOVEL IN STUNNING SHOWDOWN "Did you authorize the SEC to sue LSU and coach Lane Kiffin?" attorney Tony Clayton asked Sankey. When asked why the conference took that step, Sankey pointed to the authority of the presidents and chancellors he represents. "We established our First Amendment right for freedom of association, so that our conference can make decisions and our members can make decisions about membership," Sankey said. At that point, all options were on the table of how to move forward. Judging by the decision of LSU on Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, it was starting to become much clearer that the Tigers had finally backed down. LSU sends letter to SEC about complying with the rules The back-and-forth between all parties involved came to a head last Friday, when SEC presidents and chancellors had seen enough. At one point, a number of school officials were prepared to punish the school, with the topic of expulsion being brought up numerous times. While this never felt like a realistic option, the threat weighed heavy on the minds of folks around Baton Rouge. In a letter sent to SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey on Wednesday morning, and obtained by OutKick, LSU President Wade Rousse wanted to make it clear that the Tigers were going to comply with conference rules and not roster any of the athletes who would have been eligible under a court injunction. "On the afternoon of September 4, 2026, I called and provided you with advance notice that LSU would not place Dae'Quan Wright or Zxavian Harris on the football roster," President Rousse explained. "This was confirmed when LSU submitted its roster later that evening. On September 8, 2026, LSU filled its two remaining roster spots with eligible student-athletes. The roster is now locked for the season. "LSU complied with SEC rules. The issue is now mute." In terms of the meeting that was scheduled for Thursday between SEC presidents and chancellors to vote on what type of punishments to levy against LSU for this whole saga, President Rousse tried to make it clear that there would not be a challenge from the school, but the issue was now finalized. "Also on September 8, 2026, I received notice of the special President's and Chancellor's meeting scheduled for tomorrow, September 10, 2026. At no point has LSU ever threatened to upset that meeting," President Rousse explained. "But to be clear, LSU will not challenge, disrupt or seek to cancel or postpone this meeting. "This issue is also moot." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! LSU backed down, finally realized it wasn’t worth the fight All of this could have transpired weeks ago, when the SEC released its guidelines pertaining to rules on professional athletes returning to college sports. But, it looked as though the Tigers wanted to challenge the conference on its stance. While LSU was never actually named in the lawsuit pertaining to the athletes in a Baton Rouge court, they were certainly in the news. Thanks to statements from Governor Jeff Landry, along with Attorney General Liz Murrill showing up to the courthouse wearing a purple blouse and exclaiming 'Go Tigers' before entering the courthouse, it was obvious that while LSU officials were not present, government officials were trying to speak on their behalf. In reality, that's where this whole ordeal turned into a political sideshow that felt more like propaganda than the actual athletes involved in the case. Now, six days after the hearing inside a Baton Rouge court, the LSU Tigers are finally doing us all a favor and moving on from this nonsense that has diverted attention away from the college football season. And no, this does not mean we are done hearing about athletes from LSU being involved in legal arguments, as the school still has to make a decision on basketball player RJ Luis. articles.title: Stephen A Smith blasts SEC for threats to kick LSU out of the conference: 'Sit your a-- down'
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's bold move to bring NFL-cut players back to LSU through the transfer portal sparked SEC threats to expel the Tigers from the conference.
articles.body: The 2026 college football season is off to a surprisingly controversial start. Out of nowhere, the Western Michigan-Michigan game became one of the most contentious finishes in recent memory, with replay review adding an additional second to the fourth quarter after the game had seemingly ended. That sparked a formal appeal from the MAC to the FBS Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff to recognize the Broncos as the official winners, due to improper replay review procedures. Then there’s the human element: new LSU head coach Lane Kiffin. Kiffin drew criticism for his lengthy, drawn-out decision-making process after LSU offered him the job in Baton Rouge. His eventual decision to leave Ole Miss before the College Football Playoff made him public enemy No. 1 in Oxford. Somehow, the questions surrounding Kiffin have only deepened over time. LSU’S LANE KIFFIN FIRES BACK AT NFL RETURNEE BACKLASH: BLAME THE NCAA, NOT US FOR RECRUITING PRO ATHLETES Kiffin set about reshaping the Tigers' program through the transfer portal, then apparently had an even more unique and extreme idea: bring players who had signed with NFL teams but failed to make the regular season roster back to college football. Obviously designed to give LSU an advantage by adding more physically advanced and developed players, that tactic was immediately disparaged by opposing coaches, NFL coaches and, more importantly, the SEC itself. A war of words and policies ensued with multiple conferences, including the SEC, immediately passing a policy to prevent "pro" players returning to the collegiate ranks. LSU fought back, even winning an injunction to allow two players, Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, to confirm their eligibility. That led to some extreme measures being discussed, including reports this week that the SEC was prepared to vote imminently to expel LSU from the conference entirely. As shocking and extreme as that sounds, it's clear that the SEC wanted to ensure that their commitment to "amateur" athletics remained unblemished. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Some supported the potential vote as a punishment for Kiffin and the Tigers program pushing the limits of eligibility. And further SEC filings implied that the athletic director had little control of the football team, with Kiffin alone running the ship. But Stephen A. Smith, apparently, strongly disagrees, saying that just signing a contract in the NFL does not make you an "NFL player." "Just because you enter a draft — if you haven’t signed a contract with the NFL team, you are not an NFL player," he said during a recent episode of "First Take" on ESPN. "If you haven’t been on a practice field, if you haven’t competed against NFL players, you are not an NFL player. You should be able to go back to college. That’s the one thing that I do feel." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Smith wasn't done there, saying that LSU being pushed into independence may actually help the program. "And oh, by the way, Notre Dame, and we got love for Notre Dame, they’re an independent," he added. "LSU, you wanna throw them out the SEC? Go ahead and do it. Watch, they ain’t gonna lose. They’ll be just fine…Could you imagine Lane Kiffin as an independent? Out there in the open market for the LSU brand? Please, they’ll get paid…The SEC, sit your a-- down! Sit your a-- down!" The Tigers seemingly backed down from their plan this week, signaling by adding two other players to their roster that they wouldn't bring in those former "NFL" players. But Smith seems to have a different perspective on this than most fans or rival administrators and coaches. Once you leave college and sign with an NFL team, that's it. You're done. That's how it's always been, and changing it now opens up a can of worms. Would a player who’s, say, only made the practice squad be considered an "NFL player" in Smith’s view? Or would they still be eligible to return? What about another who is on an active roster, but never enters a game? Or someone who plays just one game before getting hurt? Defining who and who isn't a professional becomes a game of Whac-A-Mole that shouldn't be necessary. articles.title: Así serán los cuartos: España jugará en último lugar
articles.standfirst: Las eliminatorias de cuartos, las puertas para las medallas, se jugarán íntegras este jueves
articles.summary: Las eliminatorias de cuartos, las puertas para las medallas, se jugarán íntegras este jueves
articles.body: El Italia - Australia, que cerró la serie de partidos de clasificación, compuso definitivamente el cuadro de cuartos de final del Mundial, es decir, la antesala de la lucha por las medallas. Ganar el partido de cuartos implica seguir en el torneo todo el fin de semana. Perder, es sellar el billete a casa, para alguna incluso antes de lo previsto. Este jueves, el Uber Arena albergará todos los partidos de cuartos en sesión continua. Después de que la FIBA dividiera los partidos de clasificación en dos por día (martes y miércoles) obligando por ejemplo a que China y Australia no tengan ni 24 horas de descanso o a que España tuviera que esperar hasta las 22.30 para conocer a su rival, los partidos de cuartos dejarán resueltas las semifinales este jueves. Y el apasionante programa que nos espera es el siguiente: Estados Unidos - Hungría (11.30) El partido más madrugador, extrañamente de Estados Unidos, cuando los aficionados en ese país están aún durmiendo (las 05.30 hora de la Costa Este). Será el partido del turno de la mañana, con las favoritas al oro, las norteamericanas, ante la resistencia, veremos por cuánto tiempo, de las húngaras. EEUU no ha hecho un torneo redondo. Ganó con claridad a China y aplastó a la República Checa, pero estuvo a punto de perder por primera vez en 20 años en el Mundial. Lo pasó muy mal ante Italia e incluso hubo polémica en la derrota transalpina. Hungría, dos victorias y una clara derrota ante Francia, no parece un equipo hecho para derrotar a las estadounidenses, sobre todo pensando que el vigente campeón irá ajustando cada vez más su juego con la llegada de las eliminatorias directas. Tras una de las grandes favoritas al oro, la otra. Francia mide su descomunal potencial ante China que logró colarse en los cuartos merced a un ajustadísimo triunfo ante Puerto Rico. La gigante Ziyu Zhang (2,23), pondrá a prueba el potentísimo juego interior francés. El galo es probablemente el equipo que mejor ha llegado a esta cita. Eso, unido al talento de jugadoras como Gaby Williams, Marine Johannes o Dominique Malonga hace al equipo europeo muy favorito en este duelo. Entramos en un territorio más igualado, los dos partidos de cuartos con el pronóstico más incierto. Bueno, relativamente, porque Bélgica, actual campeona de Europa y un quinteto titular fabuloso, debería poner fin a la aventura de la anfitriona. La selección de Miguel Méndez se mide a un coco en estos cuartos. España hizo los deberes de quedar líder de su grupo pero con eso afronta el camino con más espinas de todos: Australia, EEUU y, si hay milagro norteamericano, Francia en la final (hipotéticamente). A pesar de las bajas de las australianas, Alanna Smith y Ezi Magbegor, el oceánico es un equipo muy potente y que arrancó este Mundial con el objetivo de una medalla. Según el ránking FIBA, Australia es la tercera del mundo, por detrás de EEUU y Francia, y por delante de España (sexta). Además las australianas han ganado los cuatro partidos que han jugado ante España en los Mundiales (4-0). Aún así, no sería una sorpresa un triunfo de España que se ha ganado por méritos propios estar en las quinielas de los equipos que llegarán a las semifinales. Será el partido que cierre los cuartos de la Copa del Mundo.

articles.title: María Conde: "El de cuartos es el partido que te marca en un campeonato"
articles.standfirst: La jugadora de la selección atiende a MARCA poco antes de medirse a Australia en el Mundial
articles.summary: La jugadora de la selección atiende a MARCA poco antes de medirse a Australia en el Mundial
articles.body: María Conde (Madrid, 1997), es una de las jóvenes veteranas de una selección que quiere buscar algo grande en el Mundial femenino. Su concurso es capital en el esquema de una España que esta noche (20.45) buscará las semifinales y con ello la lucha por las medallas ante la potente Australia. Pregunta. Lo primero, ¿cómo está? Acabó el partido ante Japón con algunas molestias físicas. Respuesta. Estoy bien. Esto es un campeonato y son partidos duros y tenemos que ir solucionando lo que va apareciendo, pero estoy bien, con ganas y contenta de que hayamos podido descansar y a esperar para empezar a jugar. P. Tras la derrota ante Mali, España vivió un primer momento crítico. ¿Cómo lo vivió el vestuario? R. Juntándonos un poco de nuevo, al final hay que confiar en el trabajo que se hace en el día a día. El baloncesto, como muchísimos otros deportes, tienes días buenos, malos y regulares. Ese día seguramente se juntaron muchas cosas que salieron muy mal y, de haber salido otras un poquito menos mal, a lo mejor el resultado habría sido distinto. Entonces era un poco juntarnos de nuevo y decir, bueno, vamos a confiar en el trabajo que estamos haciendo y enfocarnos en el partido siguiente, que es realmente lo único importante. P. También hubo un momento peligroso ante Japón al final del primer tiempo. ¿Se pensó ahí que Alemania resolvía su partido y había que ganar a toda costa? R. No, ni lo miramos ni preguntamos porque daba igual. Al final, no daba igual, evidentemente, si hubiéramos perdido, pero creo que el objetivo de todo el mundo era ganar el partido sí o sí. Por lo tanto, lo que estuviera pasando en el otro pabellón no importaba. P. Usted es una joven veterana, con kilómetros en la selección pero con mucho recorrido aún. ¿Cómo ha mezclado en su opinión la nueva generación de jugadoras? R. Creo que se ha hecho un buen trabajo intentando juntar la frescura que traen las jugadoras jóvenes, el nuevo estilo de baloncesto hacia el que yo creo que está evolucionando el deporte en sí, y eso es algo a lo que ellas se han adaptado muy bien y a lo que las jugadoras con un poco más de experiencia, a lo mejor, pues hemos tenido que ir sumando pequeñas cosas y luego, desde nuestra parte, pues intentar traer un poco la tranquilidad, a lo mejor, o la calma de haber jugado más partidos en alta competición simplemente porque tenemos más años. Y, por lo tanto, poner un poco esas cosas. Luego ya está en el cuerpo técnico el ser capaces de leer en cada partido las cosas que están funcionando y por dónde tenemos que tirar. P. ¿Se ha producido ya el cambio generacional de esta selección? R. Supongo que depende desde donde mires el inicio de ese cambio. Si contamos esos últimos años de la plata de Río, de los oros de los siguientes europeos, creo que solo queda Alba en el equipo de esos años. Entonces, seguramente se habrá producido un cambio. ¿Qué tipo de éxitos o derrotas o victorias van a venir a partir de ahí? No lo sabemos. Las generaciones que están ahora, las jugadoras que ya forman parte de la selección, vienen con mucha fuerza, jugadoras con mucha calidad y muy bien entrenadas y seguramente vengan también generaciones fuertes por debajo. Vemos los resultados que está habiendo en categorías inferiores y, por lo tanto, pues creo que cabe ser tener cierta esperanza con que se está haciendo buen baloncesto pero al final, igual que crecemos nosotros, van creciendo el resto de selecciones. Vemos a Francia, a Bélgica incluso, compitiendo también en categorías inferiores, incluso a Eslovenia, selecciones que a lo mejor no han sido tan fuertes estos últimos años a nivel senior, pero que están haciendo las cosas muy bien en categorías inferiores y eso también es un poco una marca de que otros países se están poniendo las pilas en ese sentido y, por lo tanto, lo que podamos hacer va a depender también de nosotras y de seguir viniendo aquí, seguir viniendo con ganas de trabajar y seguir encontrando por qué camino tenemos que ir. P. ¿Se han marcado un listón en este campeonato de lo que sería un gran torneo o un exitazo? R. Yo creo que un exitazo sería ganar, evidentemente, porque eso es algo con lo que soñamos todas, jugadoras, entrenadores y cuerpo técnico que estamos aquí, no sólo de nuestra selección, sino de todas las selecciones, creo que todos venimos aquí a ganar, por lo tanto ese sería el gran éxito. Pero para mí un campeonato exitoso, del que estar orgullosos, es un poco el seguir haciendo las cosas de la manera en la que las queremos hacer, el estar felices con el trabajo hecho y por lo tanto si eso es, hacer un partido muy serio en cuartos y no llevarse la victoria, pues a lo mejor eso también es un buen resultado o a lo mejor es llegar a la final habiendo pasado por encima de Estados Unidos. articles.body:
The stage is set for the final weekend of the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup with the last two teams advancing to the quarterfinals on Wednesday.

Australia and China claimed the final two spots, joining the United States, Spain, Hungary, France, Belgium and Germany in pursuit of a gold medal.

Here is the updated schedule for the four quarterfinal matchups and odds to win the tournament.

With the exception of a close call against Italy in which the offense could muster just 55 points, there has been nothing in Team USA's performance thus far to suggest it won't leave Berlin as champions.

Immediately after the scare against Italy, the Americans rebounded with a 41-point win over the Czech Republic.

The strongest challenger to the U.S. right now looks to be France, which had the best point differential of any team in group play at plus-127 in three games.

France and the United States are on opposite sides of the bracket, so a matchup wouldn't happen until the title game if it comes to pass. Team USA has never lost to France in six head-to-head meetings with the last matchup coming in group play at the 2020 Olympics.

This French roster is better than the group from Tokyo with Janelle Salaun and Dominique Malonga alongside Gabby Williams and Marine Johannès.

Team USA's overall depth gives it an advantage against anyone in the world, but another bad shooting night like the Italy game could open the door for France to end their quest for a fifth straight World Cup title that dates back to 2010.

The NBA and Nike unveiled new warmup, practice and travel gear for all 30 teams to use during the 2026-27 season in photos posted Wednesday on X.

The "NBA Standard Issue Collection" primarily features oversized team logos on hoodies, pants, t-shirts and shorts.

The collection will drop in two separate launches on Sept. 15 and Oct. 12.

It reflects insights from more than 400 high school basketball players, 100 NBA players and all 30 NBA teams as well as "players and fans from around the world," per Wednesday's announcement .

Nike Basketball creative director Ross Klein explained how the collection sought to increase the connection between fans and the game.

"Basketball is more than a game — it's a culture and a form of self-expression," Klein said as part of the announcement. "This collection celebrates the attitude, creativity and individuality of today's hoopers, combining bold team identity and modern style so fans can show their connection to the game in their own way."

Products included in the collection contain bouncy fleece to bring lightweight breathability, braided drawcords, woven labels and elevated finishes.

The designs will also be incorporated in the NBA's "Specter Edition" alternate uniforms, which have yet to be revealed.

The NBA announced Wednesday that the alternates will be given to teams that have history tracing back to the "earliest chapters of the NBA" including the Sacramento Kings, Detroit Pistons, Atlanta Hawks, Golden State Warriors, New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Los Angeles Lakers and Boston Celtics.

The 2026-27 season will begin on Oct. 20.

articles.summary: Jalen Brunson will host the "Saturday Night Live" season premiere, joining Peyton Manning, LeBron James and Michael Jordan among athlete hosts.
articles.body: The first batch of hosts for the new season of "Saturday Night Live" has been announced, and New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson is about to join an elite group of athletes who have been given the nod. A group with varying degrees of success. Brunson will host the season premiere of the long-running sketch comedy series, which — believe it or not, kids — has at times in its 50-plus-year run been very funny. That will air on September 26 with musical guest Katseye. KNICKS STAR JALEN BRUNSON IS A MAN OF THE PEOPLE, REVEALS THE ONE THING HE CAN'T LIVE WITHOUT Considering he's done some stuff with WWE, I think Brunson might be one of the athletes who actually does well on SNL. As I said, over the years, we've seen some athletes who proved to be good actors and a lot who were as stiff as a board and portrayed themselves in just about every sketch. They put out an SNL sports special back in the late aughts (I downloaded it onto my iPod Touch and would watch it in study hall; that's how late aughts it was), and you'd be surprised how many solid sketches there were with athletes, even if the athlete is not a great actor in the sketch. I think the best athlete host of all time is, without question, Peyton Manning. In fact, I've even argued that his timing is so good, he probably could've been a supporting player. His high-water mark was without a doubt the United Way commercial, one of the best commercial parodies of the last 25 years. A standard SNL play when the athlete's acting is a little on the wooden side is to put them in a sketch where the other actor does all the work. articles.title: NBA star Jaylen Brown says in ridiculous interview he's an influencer, not an entertainer for fans
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown told Mahershala Ali he refuses to be seen as just an entertainer, adding to a long history of quotes that critics call tone-deaf vanity.
articles.body: If there is one thing Jaylen Brown is truly elite at, besides turning the ball over with his left hand on a crucial drive, it is convincing himself he is the smartest guy in any room he walks into. The NBA has a long history of foolish quotes, but Jaylen routinely delivers gems so profoundly pseudo-intellectual they belong in a Hall of Fame for tone-deaf vanity. That is saying something in a league run by LeBron. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Brown, the new Sixers star, recently sat down with Oscar winner Mahershala Ali for a slick Hollywood Reporter feature, and predictable as sunrise, Brown could not stick to basketball. Instead, we got his latest sermon on why he is far too deep to be categorized as a mere athlete. "I refuse to adopt the idea that me being an athlete, I’m just here to entertain people," Brown said, apparently rebranding himself from NBA wing to sociopolitical visionary. "They want our athletes, our musicians, our entertainers, our people of influence to think that we just here for entertainment purposes. I’m going to forever disagree with that." Right. When millions of fans fork over hard-earned cash for tickets and jerseys, they aren’t looking to kick back on a Tuesday night and watch a game. They’re obviously tuning in to absorb the profound cultural wisdom of a guy making over $300 million to bounce a leather ball on hardwood. BOSTON CELTICS STAR JAYLEN BROWN TELLS ESPN'S STEPHEN A SMITH TO 'BE QUIET AND RETIRE' For years, Brown has cultivated a reputation as the league’s resident philosopher-king, masking questionable judgment behind a wall of academic posturing. "No offense to everybody in sports," Brown declared, "but the bar is f***ing low." NBA media fanboys love to brag that Brown was an "MIT Fellow." He defended Irving’s promotion of an antisemitic film, stuck by Kanye West’s Donda Sports long after everyone else fled and wore a Q-Ray-style magnetic necklace marketed as a device that could supposedly alter the body’s energy frequencies through a smartphone app. Yet Brown still expects the world to treat him like a generational thought leader who transcends basketball, all while complaining about how unfairly athletes are treated. articles.title: Josh Hart Says Knicks Using NBA Title Repeat Doubts as Fuel for 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Josh Hart chatted with play-by-play announcer Chris Fowler and analyst John McEnroe during Alexander Zverev's U.S. Open quarterfinal win over Botic van de Zandschulp on Wednesday evening.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Josh Hart chatted with play-by-play announcer Chris Fowler and analyst John McEnroe during Alexander Zverev's U.S. Open quarterfinal win over Botic van de Zandschulp on Wednesday evening.

During the talk, Fowler asked if New York was "back on the grind," noting the Knicks had a "big target" on their back after winning the championship.

Hart disagreed with the assessment and explained why.

"I don't think we have a big target," Hart said. "Because I don't think anyone is picking us to win again. We're using it as fuel. We're still the hunters. We're not satisfied with one. So we're the hunters, and we like playing that game."

Both Hart and Fowler are right in their own ways. The Knicks might have a target on their back simply for being last year's champions. It was a well-deserved title after they went 16-3 in the playoffs, including a 14-1 stretch to cap the crown.

That said, New York certainly doesn't enter the year as championship favorites. In fact, the Knicks aren't even the overwhelming favorite to win the Eastern Conference.

Looking at the title odds , per FanDuel Sportsbook, the Oklahoma City Thunder (+230) and San Antonio Spurs (+280) lead the way. The Knicks and Philadelphia 76ers are tied for third at 10-1.

The Knicks are also listed at +360 to win the East . No other team has shorter odds, but the 76ers (+400) and Boston Celtics (+550) aren't far behind, while a trio of teams looms next: the Toronto Raptors (8/1), Cleveland Cavaliers and Detroit Pistons (+850 each). So, in other words, the Eastern Conference is seen as an open race.

The Knicks deciding to see themselves as the hunters and using the fact that they aren't considered championship favorites is ultimately a good idea.

The table is set for New York to make another deep playoff run, especially after the franchise brought nearly the entire roster (including the whole starting lineup) back into the mix.

The Knicks open the season on Oct. 20 against the 76ers, who are championship contenders themselves after bringing in LeBron James and Jaylen Brown to a team that made the second round of the playoffs last year.

articles.title: US President Donald Trump drops vehement criticism on Dallas Mavericks’ Luka Doncic trade: “It might go down as the worst trade in the history of sports”
articles.summary: NBA News: The Luka Doncic trade is not winding down, as it has found a new critic. The president of the United States, Donald Trump, stopped by the Dallas Maver.
articles.body: The Luka Doncic trade is not winding down, as it has found a new critic. The president of the United States, Donald Trump, stopped by the Dallas Mavericks' home arena Wednesday night and told a packed room he still can't make sense of the deal that sent Doncic west.Trump was speaking at American Airlines Center during the Republican National Committee's midterm convention, and basketball wasn't even the point of the night. He brought it up anyway and went on to compare Dallas trading away its franchise star to one of the most infamous sales in baseball history.Donald Trump delivers harsh verdict on Luka Doncic trade 19 months laterNineteen months after the trade went through, Donald Trump stood inside the building where Doncic used to play and admitted the whole thing still baffles him. His remarks came on the opening night of the RNC's two-day midterm convention, the first time the event has been held at the Mavericks' arena. Lee Greenwood's "God Bless the USA" was still fading out as Trump walked onstage around 8:10 p.m.He was upfront about not being a basketball expert. That didn't stop him from delivering a verdict anyway. Trump said, "This is a big Dallas Mavericks team, which is going to be hopefully good. I must tell you, I don't understand the trade. That trade is not, what do I know about basketball? I would say it's not going to go down as the greatest trade in the history of sports. It might go down as the worst trade in the history of sports."Further, the President went on to compare the Red Sox-New York Yankees wild 1919 Babe Ruth trade, "Babe will always be the worst trade. But is it Luka? Maybe we could redo that trade. I redo deals all the time. We gotta redo that deal. I don't get that deal. Some deals you understand; I understand deals. But that one I didn't quite get."The trade closed on February 2, 2025, and it was bigger than a straight one-for-one swap. It was actually a three-team deal that also pulled in the Utah Jazz. Dallas sent Doncic to Los Angeles and got back Anthony Davis, Max Christie, and a 2029 first-round pick. Nine months later, the Mavericks fired general manager Nico Harrison, the man who built the trade, and handed the front office to Michael Finley and Matt Riccardi.How Luka Doncic's trade changed the Mavericks and the NBAThree months after the trade, Dallas won draft lottery luck and took Cooper Flagg first overall. Flagg started every game he played as a rookie, averaging 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.5 assists, and won Rookie of the Year. Davis lasted only 20 games in Dallas before a February 2026 trade sent him to Washington, while Christie stuck around and shot 40.4 percent from three across 77 games. The Mavericks are still in the puzzle and attempting to rebuild the roster.The Mavericks still finished 26-56. Masai Ujiri took over basketball operations in May, hired Mike Schmitz away from Portland, and parted ways with coach Jason Kidd soon after. Dusty May now runs the bench. Doncic, meanwhile, is averaging 31.9 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 8.1 assists across 92 games in Los Angeles, numbers that make Trump's frustration easy to understand, even if the front office saw it differently.Following the trade, there were huge protests by fans, and certainly, it was one of the most talked-about trades in history, as it has also garnered attention from Trump.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump pide que Dallas "deshaga" el traspaso de Doncic a los Lakers: "El peor de la historia del deporte"
articles.standfirst: Donald Trump aprovechó una convención del Partido Republicano en Dallas para criticar el traspaso de Luka Doncic de los Mavericks a los Lakers
articles.summary: Donald Trump aprovechó una convención del Partido Republicano en Dallas para criticar el traspaso de Luka Doncic de los Mavericks a los Lakers
articles.body: Donald Trump, presidente de Estados Unidos, habló sobre el traspaso de Luka Doncic desde los Dallas Mavericks a Los Angeles Lakers durante una convención del Partido Republicano en Dallas (Texas). "Este es un gran equipo, los Dallas Mavericks, que esperemos que sea bueno... Debo decirles que no entiendo el traspaso de Doncic. ¿Qué sé yo de baloncesto? Diría que eso no pasará a la historia como el mejor traspaso del deporte. Podría pasar a la historia como el peor traspaso del deporte", dijo Donald Trump. El presidente de Estados Unidos le recomendó a los Mavericks, la franquicia NBA en la que esta temporada jugarán los españoles Santi Aldama y Sergio de Larrea, que "hay que rehacerlo (el traspaso de Doncic a los Lakers)". Donald Trump, en modo analista deportivo, aseguró también que "el peor traspaso en la historia del deporte" fue el que envió a Babe Ruth de los Boston Red Sox a los New York Yankees. El 26 de diciembre de 1919 los Red Sox mandaron a Babe Ruth a los Yankees en una venta directa de 100.000 dólares en efectivo (una cifra récord para la época), acompañada de un préstamo de 300.000 dólares. Este traspaso fue el origen de la conocida como la Maldición del Bambino (los Yankees pasaron de no tener ningún título a ganar cuatro Series Mundiales con Ruth. Los Red Sox sufrieron una sequía de títulos que duró 86 años). "Lo de Babe siempre será el peor traspaso. Pero... ¿lo es el de Doncic? Eso no es bueno. ¿Fue bueno? Quizás podríamos rehacer ese traspaso. Yo rehago acuerdos todo el tiempo. Hay que rehacerlo. Hay que rehacer eso. No entiendo ese acuerdo. Saben, hay acuerdos que uno entiende. Yo entiendo de acuerdos, pero ese no terminé de entenderlo", dijo Donald Trump volviendo a sugerir a los Mavericks que deshagan el traspaso de Doncic. El 2 de febrero de 2025 una operación a tres bandas impactó a la NBA y acabó con Luka Doncic en los Lakers. Los Lakers recibieron a Luka Doncic, Maxi Kleber y Markieff Morris, los Dallas Mavericks a Anthony Davis, Max Christie y una elección de primera ronda del Draft de 2029 y los Utah Jazz a Hood-Schifino, una segunda ronda del Draft de 2025 y otra segunda ronda de 2025. Ninguno de los jugadores implicados, ni los estelares Luka Doncic y Anthony Davis, supieron nada de la operación hasta que se cerró.

articles.title: Josh Hart Responds To Knicks’ Back-To-Back Championship Doubters: ‘We’re Not Satisfied’
articles.summary: Josh Hart claps back at the Knicks' critics who feel they can't repeat their championship run in 2027.
articles.body:
The Knicks ended a 53-year championship drought with the 2026 NBA title. So it is natural for most people to wonder whether they can repeat and win back-to-back rings. NBA champion Josh Hart acknowledges that most people don't believe the Knicks can win another championship in 2027.

During an appearance at the US Open quarterfinal tennis matchup between Alexander Zverev and Botic Van de Zandschulp, Josh Hart directly addressed critics who believe the Knicks cannot repeat their championship run in 2027.

"I don't think we have a big target (on our back) because I don't think anyone is picking us to win again. So we're using it as fuel; we're still the hunters. We're not satisfied with one; the next goal is to get another. So we're the hunters, and we like playing that game," Hart said.

He also said this current Knicks roster has so much team chemistry that even non-New Yorkers respect them.

"For us, it's about helping each other. We all are high-character guys, and we realized that if everyone is willing to sacrifice, you don't have egos, and you're not selfish, then you're going to get far. You're going to get where you want to be at the end of the season," Hart added .

Several analysts and media voices argue that the Knicks had an easy route to the NBA championship in 2026. They faced inexperienced teams like the Hawks and the Spurs , and two solid teams (the 76ers and the Cavaliers ) right after grueling seven-game series in earlier rounds, giving them a fatigue-related advantage because they had more time to rest.

Moreover, they reached the NBA Finals without facing any of the top two seeds in the East (the Pistons and the Celtics ), so arguably they did not face any team that had proven they were better than them in the regular season (except the Spurs , who lacked playoff experience).

So it is understandable that critics are skeptical of the Knicks' hopes of repeating this championship run. But Josh Hart believes that the Knicks have what it takes to prove the doubters wrong.

Josh Hart is coming off a solid 2025-26 season in which he averaged 11.6 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 4.8 assists in 85 games played (including the playoffs). He shot 49.1% from the field and 39.0% from the three-point line.

Hart's comments suggest that he feels the key to the Knicks' success is their willingness to sacrifice. This summer, Hart may have to sacrifice once again off the court as the Knicks look to retain their championship-winning core while approaching the second apron .

The 31-year-old is eligible for a $132 million contract extension this summer, but reports suggest he could accept a $54 million contract to allow the Knicks to retain financial flexibility to keep the team together. That would be a $78 million sacrifice for the team.

If the Knicks manage to retain their championship core and keep them happy without breaching the second apron, they do have a chance to prove critics wrong. But if the second apron woes force the front office to make a major move, it could hurt the Knicks' championship hopes.

Therefore, it will certainly be interesting to see how the Knicks plan their championship defense in the coming 2026-27 season.
