articles.title: Former NBA journeyman makes wild ‘biggest what-if’ in league history claim
articles.summary: A former NBA player reveals what stopped him from becoming a basketball star. During the late 2000s and early 2010s, the NBA saw a change in the face of the...
articles.body:
A former NBA player reveals what stopped him from becoming a basketball star.

During the late 2000s and early 2010s, the NBA saw a change in the face of the league as the likes of LeBron James , Carmelo Anthony , and Dwyane Wade reached the prime of their respective careers.

Speaking of Anthony, he was involved in a massive trade to the New York Knicks in 2011 in a package involving former sixth overall pick Danilo Gallinari .

At the time, Gallinari was on course to become the next big thing in the NBA, but he could never reach his full potential.

Danilo Gallinari says not the NY Knicks trade, but injuries ruined his career

During a recent interview with HoopsHype , Gallinari recalled some major moments from his career, including the trade to the Denver Nuggets .

Gallinari explained how he's the 'biggest what-if' NBA star in the history of the league.

"No, I sometimes talk about it. I think about it just with friends and family when we sometimes talk about basketball and my career.

"We think about it, or when I come back to New York and I talk to my fans or people in New York that still work for the Knicks, we talk about it, but there is a lot of, unfortunately, because of my injuries, there is a lot of what-if in my career," Gallinari said.

He added, "I don't know, I'm probably the biggest what-if guy in the history of the game, maybe. But it's part of an NBA career.

"It happened to me, unfortunately, more than any other athlete probably, as far as injuries, but I don't think about it too much."

After getting traded to the Nuggets, Gallinari established himself as a stellar scorer, but injuries always held him back. Moreover, he suffered a torn ACL in 2013 that completely derailed his NBA career.

Gallinari still played in the league until the 2023-24 season, albeit as a role player for multiple franchises, and officially announced his retirement in 2025, at the age of 37.

articles.title: Carmen Hernández, al Mundial de baloncesto paralímpico ¡con 13 años!
articles.standfirst: El talento de la benjamina del equipo le ha hecho ganarse un hueco en la selección
articles.summary: El talento de la benjamina del equipo le ha hecho ganarse un hueco en la selección
articles.body: "Esta niña va a dar muchas alegrías a España, ya verás", nos avisaba hace tres años Sonia Ruiz, capitana entonces de la selección absoluta de baloncesto en silla y entrenadora de la Sub25. La murciana se refería a Carmen Hernández, una niña de 10 años que la acompañaba en su visita a MARCA junto a Vicky Vilariño, compañera de selección y también del cuerpo técnico. Unos días después viajaba a Tailandia para disputar el Mundial Sub25. Allí, España fue cuarta. El tiempo le ha dado la razón. Con 13 años, Carmen Hernández ha sido convocada por primera vez para un Mundial absoluto y nada menos que al otro lado del charco, en Ottawa (Canadá), a más de 5.000 kilómetros de España. "Carmen es puro talento, es una jugadora que pocas veces se ve”, dice Víctor Ramos, el seleccionador femenino de baloncesto paralímpico, al hablar de la benjamina del equipo. “Aún no soy muy consciente de que voy a ir a un Mundial. Al ser tan pequeña y ser tan lejos de casa todavía estoy procesándolo", reconoce. Pero tiene claro su cometido: "Mi objetivo allí es es aportar lo máximo. Todavía me veo pequeña, pero con muchas ganas de dar lo mejor”. Ya lo hizo en la repesca celebrada en Guadalajara, donde España se jugó el billete al Mundial y fue una de las protagonistas en el partido decisivo con 10 puntos y 7 asistencias. Hernández, que usa la silla de ruedas para desplazarse tras una intervención en la médula espinal que le salvó la vida antes de que cumpliese tres años, comenzó a jugar con 9-10 años. "Siempre me han gustado los deportes en equipo porque me parecen más divertidos", reconoce la joven. La murciana encontró en Beatriz Zudaire, una de las líderes de la selección, a su mentora. El UCAM Murcia, que durante años tuvo a un equipo en División de Honor con un gran número de mujeres, montó una escuela de baloncesto en silla de ruedas y Zudaire y Lourdes Ortega era las encargadas de captar nuevos talentos. Desde el primer día que probó el baloncesto en silla, quiso volver a la pista. Se convirtió en una habitual de las convocatorias de categorías inferiores de la selección y con 10 años ya fue convocada para el Mundial Sub25 de Tailandia (2023). Allí acabaron cuartas. Ahora Carmen comparte vestuario y cancha con Zudaire y con Ortega en la absoluta. La jugadora vasca la considera como su "hermana pequeña". "Es una niña con un futuro tremendo. Tiene un talento que pocas veces se ve en una jugadora de su edad. Me hace mucha ilusión compartir con ella selección. Yo la conocí cuando todavía ella no sabía ni lo que era el baloncesto adaptado", recuerda Zudaire. En la selección esperan que Ottawa sea la primera cita importante de muchas. "Mi sueño es ir a los Juegos Paralímpicos", asegura Carmen, que en la pista se hace grande. En dos años puede cumplirse.

articles.title: Australia - España: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV el partido de cuartos del Mundial de Baloncesto Femenino
articles.standfirst: Será el partido que cierre los cuartos de la Copa del Mundo
articles.summary: Será el partido que cierre los cuartos de la Copa del Mundo
articles.body: La selección española femenina de baloncesto logró su pase directo a cuartos de final después de ganar a Japón en el último encuentro de la fase de grupos por 59-79. Afronta este decisivo cruce de cuartos de final tras dos días de descanso. El combinado de Miguel Méndez terminó primero del grupo A, con dos victorias (ante Alemania y Japón) y una derrota (contra Mali). Hasta última hora de este miércoles España no conoció al que será su rival en los cuartos que se tienen que jugar menos de 24 horas después. Y será Australia el equipo que se mida a las españolas buscando un lugar en la lucha por las medallas. La selección de Miguel Méndez se mide a un coco en estos cuartos. España hizo los deberes de quedar líder de su grupo pero con eso afronta el camino con más espinas de todos: Australia, EEUU y, si hay milagro norteamericano, Francia en la final (hipotéticamente). A pesar de las bajas de las australianas, Alanna Smith y Ezi Magbegor, el oceánico es un equipo muy potente y que arrancó este Mundial con el objetivo de una medalla. Según el ránking FIBA, Australia es la tercera del mundo, por detrás de EEUU y Francia, y por delante de España (sexta). Además las australianas han ganado los cuatro partidos que han jugado ante España en los Mundiales (4-0). Aún así, no sería una sorpresa un triunfo de España que se ha ganado por méritos propios estar en las quinielas de los equipos que llegarán a las semifinales. Será el partido que cierre los cuartos de la Copa del Mundo. Sobre el rival, el seleccionador español Miguel Méndez aseguró que "tienen jugadoras muy fuertes, con experiencia, muchas jugando en WNBA y es un equipo muy duro físicamente, pero vamos a intentar que se adapten a nuestro estilo". El partido entre Australia y España de los cuartos de final del Mundial de Baloncesto Femenino se juega hoy, jueves 10 de septiembre, a las 20.45 horas. El encuentro se podrá ver por los canales M+ Vamos, M+ #Vamos Bar y M+ Baloncesto, de la plataforma Movistar Plus. También se podrá ver por Teledeporte y por su página web, RTVE Play. Además, se puede ver por la plataforma DAZN. Sigue toda la actualidad del Mundial de Baloncesto femenino, el minuto a minuto del Australia - España y la mejor crónica del partido en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Estados Unidos tritura a Hungría y ya espera a España en las semifinales
articles.standfirst: Las estadounidenses resolvieron en el primer cuarto (36-12) en un partido que fue un entrenamiento
articles.summary: Las estadounidenses resolvieron en el primer cuarto (36-12) en un partido que fue un entrenamiento
articles.body: Un entrenamiento con público. Eso es lo que fue el partido ante Hungría para unos Estados Unidos que trituró al equipo europeo 108-56, y selló su billete para las semifinales jugando además en tercera velocidad, sin un excesivo gasto de energías. Hungría dispuso de la primera posesión para dominar el marcador, pero Réka Lelik falló una bandeja más o menos fácil. Fue el preludio del vendaval que a partir de ahí sufriría Hungría, que se llegó a poner 2-3 en su única ventaja del partido. Su liderato duró 19 segundos. Aunque EEUU empezó con cierta frialdad, fue cogiendo ritmo hasta alcanzar una velocidad de crucero que le llevó a tener el choque sentenciado, 36-12, cuando se había esfumado el primer cuarto. Napheesa Collier y Breanna Stewart eran las que más daños estaban haciendo a la defensa húngara. Hungría se había entregado casi desde el inicio, sabedora de que no podrían competir contra el gran favorito. En parte por una defensa muy permisiva y en parte porque las estadounidenses tuvieron un gran día en el tiro, EEUU llevaba al descanso porcentajes fabulosos en tiros de dos (18/26, 69%) y en tiros de tres (6/11, 55%). Hungría, con 14 pérdidas (8 robos rivales), se veía abajo al descanso por casi 30 (59-30). La ventaja norteamericana no dejó de crecer en un segundo tiempo de puro trámite. Estados Unidos seguía siendo una apisonadora a pesar de jugar a medio gas y Hungría trataba de capear el temporal como podía. Sin las exigencias del rival, EEUU freno algo más su ritmo para no hacer más daño que los 52 puntos finales (la máxima fue 53). EEUU jugó con el freno de mano el tramo final. Napheesa Collier acabó como la mejor anotadora del partido con 19 puntos y además 6 rebotes, Rhyne Howard hizo 15 y Jackie Young y Kahleah Coper, 10 cada una. EEUU ni siquiera necesitó la mejor versión de Caitlin Clark, que hizo también 10 puntos y 6 asistencias algo más entonada que en otros partidos. Estados Unidos espera ahora rival en semifinales que, si se cumplen los pronósticos, podría ser España. Las norteamericanas llegan con tres plácidas victorias y el susto ante Italia como toque de atención para los dos duelos que les quedan en el torneo.

articles.title: Partizan de Fuenlabrada: nuevo nombre para una hermandad histórica
articles.standfirst: Esa será desde hoy la denominación del club madrileño para unir sus destinos al club serbio 35 años después
articles.summary: Esa será desde hoy la denominación del club madrileño para unir sus destinos al club serbio 35 años después
articles.body: El círculo se cierra 35 años después. Baloncesto Fuenlabrada pasa a llamarse Partizan de Fuenlabrada, una nueva denominación que culmina una relación histórica nacida en 1991. Aquel año, con la guerra en la antigua Yugoslavia, el Partizan de Belgrado convirtió Fuenlabrada en su casa para disputar como local la Copa de Europa 91/92. Y allí, juntos, acabaron tocando el cielo: campeones de Europa. Ahora, aquella historia de acogida, solidaridad y éxito da un paso más. Partizan de Fuenlabrada nace como un proyecto común entre dos clubes unidos por mucho más que el baloncesto. La alianza se extiende a los ámbitos institucional, deportivo, social, de negocio y de marca, con la ambición de convertir aquella hermandad forjada hace 35 años en un motor de crecimiento para ambos. Porque hablar del Partizan en Fuenlabrada es hablar de una historia compartida que trascendió las pistas. Es hablar de valores, de gratitud y de la capacidad de sobreponerse a las dificultades. La relación que comenzó en uno de los momentos más complicados de la historia del club balcánico no se quedó en aquella temporada: se mantuvo viva durante décadas y se ha intensificado especialmente en los últimos años. Ahora comienza un nuevo capítulo. Ya están en marcha proyectos conjuntos para la formación de jugadores, iniciativas institucionales y acciones destinadas a potenciar y revalorizar la marca. El Partizan de Fuenlabrada recoge así el legado de aquel equipo que hizo historia en 1992 y lo proyecta hacia el futuro. Una alianza nacida de la necesidad que, 35 años después, se convierte en una apuesta de futuro.

articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “We really had an amazing love story” How Kobe Bryant and Vanessa rebuilt their marriage and held on to love through life’s hardest moments
articles.summary: NBA News: Kobe Bryant's life was filled with championships, records and unforgettable moments, but his family remained at the centre of it all. He met Vanessa B.
articles.body: Kobe Bryant's life was filled with championships, records and unforgettable moments, but his family remained at the centre of it all. He met Vanessa Bryant in 1999, married her in 2001 and together they raised four daughters. Their marriage went through a difficult period, but they eventually reconciled and continued their life together.Years later, Vanessa looked back on their relationship with words that captured what their life together meant to her. “We really had an amazing love story,” she said at Kobe and Gianna Bryant’s 2020 memorial. How did Kobe Bryant and Vanessa Bryant’s love story begin?Kobe and Vanessa met in November 1999 while Vanessa was still a high-school student and Kobe was already an NBA star. Their relationship moved quickly, and within six months they were engaged. They married on April 18, 2001, at St. Edward the Confessor Catholic Church in Dana Point, California.Their early years together came while Kobe was becoming one of basketball’s biggest names. Away from the court, though, their relationship was much more private. They eventually became parents to four daughters, Natalia, Gianna, Bianka and Capri, and Kobe became known for the way closely he embraced his role as a father.Vanessa later described Kobe as much more than the basketball player the world knew. During the 2020 memorial, she said he was her “first girlfriend, his first love, his wife, his best friend,” describing the relationship they had built from their teenage years into adulthood.Their life was not perfect, however. In December 2011, Vanessa filed for divorce, citing irreconcilable differences. After more than a decade together, the couple appeared to be heading in separate directions.But the story did not end there. In January 2013, Kobe and Vanessa announced that they had reconciled and would dismiss the divorce proceedings. Their joint statement was simple: “We are looking forward to our future together.” They chose to continue their marriage and family life rather than walk away from what they had built.That decision became an important part of their story because the years that followed were filled with family milestones. Kobe eventually retired from the NBA in 2016, giving him more time with his daughters and allowing him to take on an even bigger role at home. What did Kobe Bryant and Vanessa Bryant’s marriage mean to them?Vanessa's memories of Kobe showed that their relationship was not built only around grand romantic gestures. She remembered the small traditions, anniversary trips and thoughtful gifts that Kobe planned during their marriage.At the memorial, Vanessa revealed one particularly memorable gift. Kobe had given her the actual notebook and the blue dress worn by Rachel McAdams in “The Notebook”. When she asked why he chose the dress, Kobe explained that it represented the moment when Allie returned to Noah.Vanessa then connected the movie to their own relationship. “We had hoped to grow old together like the movie,” she said. “We really had an amazing love story.”Those words became even more emotional because Kobe had been thinking about their future shortly before his death. Vanessa recalled that he had sent her a text saying he wanted them to spend time together, just the two of them.The couple had spent years raising their daughters and managing their responsibilities, so Kobe was already looking ahead to another stage of their life. Vanessa said he wanted to renew their vows, travel the world together and eventually become grandparents.“He would have been the coolest grandpa,” Vanessa said while remembering the future they had imagined.For Vanessa, those plans showed that Kobe was still thinking about their relationship beyond basketball. His career had ended, their children were growing older and the couple had another chapter they wanted to experience together.That chapter never came. How did Vanessa Bryant carry their family forward after Kobe’s death?Kobe and 13-year-old Gianna were among nine people killed in a helicopter crash in January 2020. The tragedy changed Vanessa's life completely, leaving her to raise their surviving daughters while also dealing with the loss of her husband and daughter.At the memorial, Vanessa spoke about the future Kobe would never get to see. He would not walk their daughters down the aisle, travel with her or become the grandfather they had imagined becoming.Yet she also focused on the person Kobe had been inside their home.“He was my sweet husband, and the beautiful father of our children,” Vanessa said. “He was mine. He was my everything.”She remembered how Kobe encouraged their daughters, taught them to be brave and pushed them to keep going when life became difficult. That part of his personality became especially important for Vanessa in the years that followed.Rather than allowing the loss to erase what Kobe and Gianna had built, Vanessa continued to carry their names forward. She became involved in preserving Kobe's work and helped continue the mission of the Mamba & Mambacita Foundation, while also remaining focused on her daughters and their future.Vanessa later explained how she managed to keep moving through grief. In a 2021 interview with PEOPLE, she said Kobe and Gigi motivated her to keep going and to try to be better each day. She also spoke about getting out of bed for her girls and trying to make the day better for them and herself.That is perhaps what makes Kobe and Vanessa's story so emotional. It was not a perfect relationship, and it did not have a perfect ending. They were two people who met young, built a family, faced serious difficulties, found their way back to each other and continued making plans for the future.Vanessa's description of them as “two perfectly imperfect people making a beautiful family” says more about their relationship than any championship or public achievement ever could.For Kobe, basketball was his greatest professional achievement. For Vanessa, the family they created together was something far more personal. And even after losing Kobe and Gianna, she chose to carry that family forward, keeping their memories and the life they built together at the heart of everything that came next.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Caitlin Clark-Angel Reese connection, Napheesa Collier's breakout highlight Team USA's FIBA World Cup quarterfinal win vs. Hungary
articles.summary: The on-court connection between Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese sparked brighter than any other on a pre-dawn tip-off in the U.S.
articles.body:
Team USA left nothing to chance in its 34th consecutive World Cup victory on Thursday in Berlin, Germany. The rout was over nearly as soon as it began in a suffocating 108-56 win over Hungary to reach the semifinals and continue the quest for a fifth consecutive World Cup gold.

The U.S. will face the winner of Spain vs. Australia, the final game of the quarterfinals to be played on Thursday. Matchups between China and France, and Belgium and Germany, are on the other side of the bracket.

The record-shattering win took the same path as those before it in this tournament. Head coach Kara Lawson rolled out her veterans to start, and finished with the young, up-and-coming crew to boost the lead further. The 108 points were the most by a team in a quarterfinal game in World Cup history, and tied for second-most in a knockout game at the World Cup.

More unreal stats are below, as well as takeaways from Team USA's statement victory.

Caitlin Clark-Angel Reese connection thriving

The on-court connection between Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese sparked brighter than any other on a pre-dawn tip-off in the U.S.

Clark found Reese three times in about five minutes for buckets in the second quarter that helped pad the lead. And in the second half, Reese returned the favor, assisting Clark on a bucket off the steal.

"We've played against each other so many times, so I'm sure we know each other's game like the back of each other's hands," Reese said on the post-game broadcast interview. "It's fun. We just continue to build chemistry because we know we're going to be USA teammates for a while."

Clark's version of Team USA is a highly successful (and incredibly fun to watch) run-and-gun offense that Reese fits into well. She can run the floor and is shooting more efficiently, entering the game at 57.1% through three games. The chemistry blossoming between different iterations of Clark, Reese, Paige Bueckers and Aliyah Boston will be the future, potentially as soon as the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Clark scored 10 points in a game-high 20 minutes. She had 9 assists, 3 rebounds, 2 steals and 3 turnovers. Reese scored nine, shooting 80% (4-5) with 6 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 steals, 1 block and 2 turnovers.

Their 31 assists were the most in a quarterfinal game, and the U.S. did it on 40 made baskets. No matter the lineup on the floor, the ball moved multiple times to a more wide-open shooter. They shot 59% from the floor, consisting of 52% inside the arc and 52% from outside it. The team went 12 of 23 from the perimeter, led by Rhyne Howard (3 of 5), Kahleah Copper (2 of 2), Chelsea Gray (2 of 2) and Boston (2 of 3).

The 108 points scored tied the second-most in a knockout game with the 1986 U.S. team that defeated the Soviet Union in the final. The U.S. holds the top five spots behind Brazil's total of 110 points over the U.S. in the 1994 semifinals. Every player scored, and five were in double digits. Howard scored 15, while Copper and Jackie Young chipped in 10 apiece.

The 59-30 halftime lead marked a record for first-half point totals in a quarterfinal, while Team USA's 59 points were its best after 20 minutes of any knockout game at the World Cup. The 29-point margin at the half was the largest of any previous World Cup quarterfinal game.

The final winning margin blew out that of France over Hungary. The French are favored to give the U.S. a run for the title, and moved up into the No. 1 spot in the Women's World Cup power rankings after the U.S. narrowly escaped Italy in the group stage.

Collier played the role of pace car for Team USA. She scored 10 points in the first quarter to spell a 36-12 lead and finished with a team-high 19, shooting 69% with 6 rebounds and 1 block.

Collier subbed out at the first mark for Boston, but quickly returned and ran up the score in a lineup with Boston, Clark, Young and Paige Bueckers. She took advantage of attention on Boston in the paint, hitting open layups, and utilized feeds from Clark. She and Breanna Stewart have thrived with the younger group.

The WNBA MVP runner-up only returned to 5-on-5 action in July after surgeries on both of her ankles. The World Cup is serving as a ramp-up to peak in the WNBA playoffs and potentially lead the Lynx to a record fifth WNBA championship.

Heading to Germany without four-time WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson was a loss, but not one the U.S. couldn't absorb. There is no nation deeper in talent, and Team USA showcased it with a suffocating paint presence against Hungary's frontcourt tandem of Dorka Juhasz and Virag Takacs-Kiss.

The U.S. led in paint points, 20-0, at one point and finished the half leading 32-4. They scored more in the paint than Hungary did as they built a 59-30 halftime lead. By game's end, it was up to 52-16. The U.S. won the boards, 49-29.

Juhasz and Takacs-Kiss were each held to two points apiece and 12 combined rebounds, sharply below their three-game World Cup averages. Juhasz averaged 15.3 points, shooting 50% and a third-best 15.2 rebounds per game. She was 1 of 12 against Team USA, and her Lynx teammate, Collier. Takacs-Kiss averaged 14 points and 13.7 rebounds per game, fifth in the tournament.

It left Hungary to 28 3-point attempts, of which they made 9. Reka Lelik led Hungary with 12 points. Agnes Torok scored 11.

Will Lawson ever tweak the starting lineup?

The quarterfinal against an overmatched Hungary team presented the perfect opportunity for Lawson to tweak the starting lineup. That she didn't indicates she won't at all through the rest of this tournament.

The lineup at tip remained the national team veterans: Gray, Young, Copper, Collier and Stewart. They again set the tone for the younger, inexperienced group to run away with it. Even if Lawson has to make an early substitution — which also seems unlikely — she appears set on giving the vets the honor in a "it's working" mentality.

They went up 13-7 when Lawson subbed Boston in for Collier. Bueckers came in off the bench next for Copper, and Clark in at 4:07 for Gray with USA holding an 18-9 lead.

Lawson didn't go completely young until the 4:02 mark of the third quarter and a 78-37 lead. The vets didn't see the court again.

articles.body:
D uke coach Kara Lawson is coaching Team USA in the FIBA World Cup, and while the U.S. is favored, the team has been a bit up and down. They blew out China in the opener, 94-61, nipped Italy in the second game, 55-52, then blew out Czechia in the third game, 105-64.

People online are giving Kara Lawson guff because the U.S. is not crushing everyone, and are questioning her rotation choices.

If it all works out and the U.S. wins gold, it's not an important issue.

If they fall short, though, people will never let it go.

However, defense, ball movement, and three-point shooting are all going to be critical, and all three are points of emphasis for Lawson. As long as her team does those things and plays with passion, as she asked, we can live with whatever happens.

articles.title: Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark just gave the basketball world exactly what it needed
articles.summary: Team USA stars Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark have developed an incredible on-court relationship at the World Cup, and it was on full display against Hungary...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark dribbled out the clock at the end of the third quarter of Team USA's World Cup quarterfinals game against Hungary while Angel Reese flashed to the middle of the point. Clark hit her with a perfect pass, and Reese powered her way to the basket to beat the end-of-quarter buzzer.

It was a simple play, and it was inconsequential in the scheme of the tournament — USA ultimately blew out Hungary 108-56 — but it perfectly captured the rising synergy between two of the game's youngest (and most polarizing) stars, Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark and Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese.

Clark and Reese are rivals in the WNBA, but for two weeks, they are Team USA teammates chasing gold together. And while in the media, plenty of negativity has surrounded their relationship, on the court in Berlin, their chemistry has been a thing of beauty.

In their first World Cup, both players have been standouts for Team USA. In the quarterfinals win over Hungary, Clark finished with 10 points, 9 assists, and 3 rebounds, and Reese finished with 9 points, 6 rebounds, and 3 assists. Throughout the tournament, Clark has been Team USA's top playmaker, while Reese has been among the team's most consistent rebounders. Both players are coming off the bench, but have been among the team's most impactful.

What's been most impressive is their on-court connection. Clark found Reese for easy baskets multiple times on Thursday, and Reese did the same. Clark has a knack for finding Reese on the roll; Reese is able to catch tough passes from one of the best playmakers in the sport.

And years of competing against each other both in college and in the WNBA are paying off.

"We've played against each other so many times," Reese said after the game. "So I'm sure we know each other's game — like the back of each other's hand. So I just easily dished it off to her. She dished it off to me. She knows my slides. I kind of got one to her today, or maybe two. So it's fun."

Team USA is going to rely on the duo's on-court connection as they pursue a gold medal. On Saturday, in the semi-finals, they'll face the winner of Thursday's quarterfinals game between Spain and Australia.

Reese and Clark will soon return to the WNBA to resume the 2026 regular season ahead of the postseason. But before that, they have the opportunity to add to their respective collection of hardware, and to do so together.

"We just continue to build chemistry because we know we're going to be USA teammates for a while," Reese said.

articles.title: Why Warriors fans are freaking out over a 21-second Stephen Curry video
articles.summary: A lot of theories were launched by NBA and Warriors fans alike after seeing Stephen Curry walk with a limp in Beijing amid his Li-Ning Wide Open Tour.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry remains one of the biggest NBA offseason stories yet to be resolved. The Golden State Warriors have already reached out with an extension and a full roster so he can decide, but he still hasn't chosen. Adding injury rumors makes this situation even more peculiar as the summer goes on. The fact that a video of him in Beijing for the Li-Ning Wide Open Tour is circulating hasn't helped at all. In fact, it has made speculations spread like wildfire.

Warrior' Curry sends NBA fans into injury speculation spiral amid limp

Li-Ning has brought Stephen Curry to China. He will be in the country from September 9 to 14, planning to tour major areas like Beijing, Dongguan, and Shenzhen. The Warriors star will also stop in Hong Kong during the Wide Open Tour after not being there in a little over a decade. Unexpectedly, NBA fans are excited to see the legendary sharpshooter in their areas. However, there is one big drawback.

Curry was just seen in Beijing. Everything would be fine for the Warriors and NBA fans, but the legend was limping a bit.

A whole lot of speculation has been thrown around, especially ones that posit that he could be injured.

"Father time about to claim another one. The walk shows the joint mileage," an NBA fan declared.

Another took the path of better wisdom, "This is quite normal. That age is kicking in. Everyone knows how that first step goes after you get up from sitting down have long periods of time. Those joints got tons of mileage…"

"He's going in for a workout if he was cooked he ain't working out. It's in the morning with no stretching. Thats what athletes look like

overacting for no reason," another Warriors fan added .

There is no official report from Li-Ning, the Warriors, and Curry's camp to sufficiently say that this is the case. He was suffering runner's knee for a bit throughout the 2025-26 NBA season but that got resolved.

All of this could either just be pains from a recent intense workout or just the numbing pain of what could be a really long car ride. In either scenario, there is not much cause for worry when it comes to Curry. Well, aside from not yet signing a possible two-year $136.7 million deal with the Warriors.

articles.title: Spurs Guard Dylan Harper Dismisses Comparisons to Magic Johnson, Shares 1 Crucial Thing He Learned From Recent Finals Run
articles.summary: Dylan Harper has been compared to several NBA all-time greats despite being only in his rookie season last year. The San Antonio Spurs‘ No. 2 overall pick in...
articles.body:
Dylan Harper has been compared to several NBA all-time greats despite being only in his rookie season last year. The San Antonio Spurs ' No. 2 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft was compared to James Harden because he is a left-handed guard, just like the 2018 MVP.

He was also compared to Spurs legend Manu Ginobili because of his explosiveness and his role as a guard playing alongside Victor Wembanyama , who himself has been compared to Tim Duncan .

Now, the 20-year-old is being compared to another NBA great, and this one probably came out of left field. The only point of comparison is their respective Finals runs during their rookie seasons.

Wembanyama was undeniably the best player on the Spurs' roster. He led his team to an NBA Finals appearance, won Defensive Player of the Year, and finished as a top-three MVP candidate while doing so.

The only problem was that the Spurs lost to the New York Knicks in five games, with their lack of maturity and late-game decision-making being among the main reasons for the defeat.

Harper, however, has been spared from similar criticism. Many believed he was the most composed player on the floor for coach Mitch Johnson. There were even calls for him to become a starter after his efficient performances.

He averaged 18.0 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 3.0 assists per game, numbers that were enough for some to compare him to Magic Johnson, who won Finals MVP as a rookie in 1980 after leading the Los Angeles Lakers to a championship over the Philadelphia 76ers .

Dylan Harper on Magic Johnson comparisons

Johnson remains the only rookie to win Finals MVP in NBA history. Harper reached a similar level during his team's playoff run, but the Spurs ultimately fell short.

That is where the two situations differ. The Spurs' incoming sophomore was aware of the comparisons being made, but he insisted that their circumstances were different.

Still, Harper believes there is something he can learn from Johnson's rookie Finals run.

"Yeah, definitely. But a little different, he won, you know. He had the Finals MVP. He had all that," Harper said during an interview with Scoop Robinson.

"But I think, just in a sense, I can compare my Finals run to his run and just see the things that he did to make himself successful. And I think that's probably what I've taken most from it."

Johnson averaged 21.5 points , 11.2 rebounds, and 8.7 assists per game during his rookie Finals campaign.

Harper no longer has a chance to win the Rookie Finals MVP, but he can still accomplish plenty more. The Spurs are already projected to be among the top contenders for the 2026-27 season, with Harper, Wembanyama, and Stephon Castle expected to be at the center of their success.

articles.title: NBA Draft Pick Trey Kaufman-Renn Granted  6th Year of NCAA Eligibility, Enters Transfer Portal
articles.summary: As college football is trying to navigate a situation with players drafted into the NFL coming back, college basketball has been thrust into the same situation with Minnesota Timberwolves draftee Trey Kaufman-Renn.
articles.body:
As college football is trying to navigate a situation with players drafted into the NFL coming back, college basketball has been thrust into the same situation with Minnesota Timberwolves draftee Trey Kaufman-Renn.

Per Nathan Baird of the Indianapolis Star , Kaufman-Renn has been granted a temporary restraining order against the NCAA that will make him eligible for a sixth year in college basketball.

Baird noted the judge's ruling means the NCAA can't deny Kaufman-Renn's "eligibility based on his five years in college and four years playing for the Boilermakers, or his professional status."

Kaufman-Renn, who was selected with the No. 59 overall pick by the Timberwolves in June's draft, filed a lawsuit in August seeking an additional year of college eligibility.

He will now enter the transfer portal, according to ESPN's Jeff Borzello .

Even though Kaufman-Renn arrived at Purdue for the 2021-22 season, he redshirted and didn't appear in a game his first year. He appeared in 147 games for the Boilermakers over the next four seasons.

Under the NCAA's age-based eligibility rule , student-athletes who enter college no later than the academic year after their 19th birthday will have up to five years of eligibility.

Kaufman-Renn's argument was based around the rule and if it had been in place when he originally got to Purdue that he wouldn't have had to sit during his true freshman season.

Baird noted there is currently no set date for a preliminary injunction hearing.

It's unclear where Kaufman-Renn intends to play college basketball, assuming he remains eligible when the 2026-27 season begins. He wrote on his Instagram Story after Wednesday's ruling that his time at Purdue "has come to an end" and he is "excited for what's next."

Kaufman-Renn made the All-Big Ten first team as a junior during the 2024-25 season. He averaged 11.3 points and 5.2 rebounds per game over the course of his four seasons at Purdue.

articles.summary: The United States and France punched their tickets to the semifinals of the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup on Thursday.
articles.body:
The United States and France punched their tickets to the semifinals of the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup on Thursday.

Neither team encountered much resistance in the quarterfinals, living up to their status as the two best countries in the women's game.

Here's what you need to know for the next round, which tips off Saturday.

France nearly pushed the United States to overtime in gold medal game at the 2024 Summer Olympics. A matter of inches was the difference between Gabby Williams' buzzer-beater forcing an extra period and the host country settling for a heartbreaking defeat.

The United States looked sluggish in a 55-52 win over Italy in the group phase, and that might've been the wakeup call the team needed. Team USA hammered Czechia by 41 points in its next game and won by a 52-point margin in the quarterfinals over Hungary.

Napheesa Collier scored a game-high 19 points Thursday, and Caitlin Clark narrowly missed out on another double-double (10 points and nine assists).

France was even more dominant in the group, winning its three games by a combined 127 points. The quarterfinals were more of the same.

The French held a five-point lead after the first quarter before outscoring China 23-11 in the second quarter. They sailed to a 90-61 win from there, with Marine Johannes, Gabby Williams and Janelle Salaün all scoring in double figures.

Host Germany won't be a pushover in the semis.

Buoyed by a raucous crowd in Berlin, Olaf Lange's squad dispatched of reigning European champion Belgium, overcoming a 29-point effort by 2019 WNBA Finals MVP Emma Meesseman.

Six players scored in double figures for Germany, and no star shined brither than Leonie Fiebich. She had a team-high 17 points and 10 rebounds, one of two German players to post a double-double alongside Nyara Sabally (16 points and 12 boards).

Even with Germany's strong performance, a United States vs. France final is the likely outcome from Saturday's games. The talent with both teams is too much to overlook.

articles.title: Everything Angel Reese Said About Caitlin Clark, 'Dialed In' USA After 52-Point Win at World Cup
articles.summary: Team USA defeated Hungary 108-56 in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup quarterfinals on Thursday in Berlin.
articles.body:
Team USA defeated Hungary 108-56 in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup quarterfinals on Thursday in Berlin.

After the game, Team USA forward Angel Reese spoke with TNT Sports' Allie LaForce, who asked about her chemistry with guard Caitlin Clark:

"We've played against each other so many times, so I'm sure we know each other's game like the back of each other's hand," Reese said.

"So just easily dishing off to her, she dishes off to me. She knows my spots, I kind of got one to her today, or maybe two.

"So it's fun. We just continue to build chemistry because we know we're going to be USA teammates for a while."

As LaForce noted, Team USA's 31 assists is a FIBA World Cup quarterfinal record. Clark led the way with nine dimes, including three leading to Reese buckets.

Reese also had three assists, including one to Clark.

"Everybody's just all dialed in offensively and defensively," Reese told reporters . "We talked about our keys, what it's going to take to win gold, and I think tonight we did everything that coach asked us to do."

Team USA advanced to Saturday's semifinals, where the 4-0 squad will await Thursday's quarterfinal winner of Australia vs. Spain.

articles.title: NaVorro Bowman Jr., 5-Star Guard and Son of 49ers Legend, Announces CBB Commitment
articles.summary: Five-star combo guard NaVorro Bowman Jr. committed to UConn on Thursday, according to multiple reports.
articles.body:
Five-star combo guard NaVorro Bowman Jr. committed to UConn on Thursday, according to multiple reports .

Bowman, the son of former NFL linebacker NaVorro Bowman, is the No. 11 overall player in 247Sports' composite rankings for 2027. He's the highest-ranked recruit from the class to have committed to a school so far.

D1 basketball coach shares cancer diagnosis

247Sports director of scouting Adam Finkelstein evaluated Bowman in July. He called the 6'3" guard a "volume scorer" and "true three-range threat":

"He handles, has stop-and-go change of pace, sharp changes of direction, a good left hand, and the physicality to initiate and absorb contact. He's a tough shot-maker off the dribble, with pull-up range that now extends well beyond the arc, and while there are still times he can settle (33% from three on 6+ attempts per game), he can also make shots in bunches. His ability to pressure the rim and make plays has improved significantly. He can not only get downhill with real force, but he's a quality passer when he wants to be, albeit still somewhat turnover prone at times (2.3 per game)."

247Sports' Travis Branham chimed in to say this should be a perfect fit for player and team:

Bowman showcased his skills this summer at the FIBA U17 World Cup. He averaged 11.9 points and 3.6 assists as the United States went on to win an eighth straight gold medal.

Bowman's father was a decorated star on the gridiron. NaVorro Sr. was a three-time Pro Bowler and four-time All-Pro during a seven-year career, the bulk of which came on the San Francisco 49ers.

The elder Bowman had some skills of his own, though. He was teammates with 16-time NBA All-Star Kevin Durant in middle school.

UConn didn't have a banner year on the recruiting trail during the last cycle. The Huskies finished 23rd in 247Sports' composite team rankings .

Getting Bowman's commitment is a great way for coach Dan Hurley and his staff to starting building for 2027.

articles.title: Bradley Beal Says Chris Paul's Legacy Can't Be 'Erased' After Switching to No. 3 Clippers Jersey
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers have apparently given Chris Paul's old No. 3 to Bradley Beal, who said Thursday that the iconic point guard's legacy "can't be touched, nor erased."
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers have apparently given Chris Paul's old No. 3 to Bradley Beal, who said Thursday that the iconic point guard's legacy "can't be touched, nor erased."

NBA numerologist Etienne Catalan broke the news earlier Thursday morning. Beal's No. 3 jersey is currently being sold in the Clippers' online store.

Paul revealed last February on 7PM in Brooklyn that Clippers president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank told him before he was sent home in December that L.A. would retire his number.

Perhaps a jersey number retirement still happens down the line, but it doesn't appear imminent.

The 14-year veteran wore No. 3 for the first 13 seasons of his career with the Washington Wizards and Phoenix Suns. He signed with the Clippers on July 18. Three days later, Paul returned to Los Angeles after playing one season with the San Antonio Spurs.

During his previous stint with the Clippers (2011-12 to 2016-17), Paul averaged 19.9 points, 10.4 assists and 2.3 steals per game. He was an All-NBA First Teamer for three seasons and an All-NBA Second Teamer for two. In addition, CP3 made the All-NBA First Team Defense in each of those campaigns.

L.A. won 51 or more games in his final five seasons (the 2011-12 Clippers went 40-26 in a lockout-shortened year) and made the playoffs each time.

Paul noted recently on the Build or Break podcast with Daniel Lubetzky (46:28 mark) that his exit was "probably one of the most disrespectful things that I've endured."

One can guess the decision to give away No. 3 may continue that perceived disrespect, although in theory, the Clippers could (and should) retire the number down the road.

articles.title: New Jalen Duren Rumors Update Contract Talks, Pistons Future After Receiving Qualifying Offer
articles.summary: The start of the Detroit Pistons' 2026-27 season is less than one month away, and big man Jalen Duren still doesn't have a new deal.
articles.body:
The start of the Detroit Pistons' 2026-27 season is less than one month away, and big man Jalen Duren still doesn't have a new deal.

NBA insider Marc Stein reported Thursday that "Duren is increasingly prepared to play out the coming season on his $9.6 million qualifying offer—with the intent to become an unrestricted free agent next summer—if no deal with Detroit materializes by the end of September."

Stein explained that Duren is looking for a "lucrative" five-year deal, although "there is no team in the marketplace with salary cap space to make a run at Duren that exerts pressure on the Pistons to increase their offers."

On the surface, a 22-year-old who was just selected to the All-NBA Third Team for the club that finished with the best record in the Eastern Conference having to go with the qualifying offer would be a rather shocking development.

Logic would dictate someone with that profile would get a number of lucrative offers, including one from the team that he's played for during the last four years.

The Memphis product was also a double-double machine who averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds while shooting 65 percent from the field. He also finished 11th in Defensive Player of the Year voting, underscoring his ability to impact the game in a number of ways.

However, the narrative around Duren changed drastically in the playoffs.

He became nearly unplayable for stretches in Detroit's second-round loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers. His poor outside shooting allowed Cleveland defenders to easily help off him and cut off driving lanes for Cade Cunningham. His poor free-throw shooting also became an issue at times.

It wasn't just the inability to space the floor, as he wasn't as effective on the glass as he normally is and tallied four rebounds in Game 3, two rebounds in Game 4 and five rebounds in Game 5.

It was easy to question how much a player like Duren elevates the ceiling for a championship contender in the aftermath of the playoff loss, especially in the modern-day game that is so reliant on spacing the floor on the offensive end.

With that as the backdrop, the deals he was looking for simply haven't come in this offseason. And he may find himself playing on the qualifying offer as a result.

articles.title: New Kawhi Leonard Rumors Reveal Raptors Are 'Eager' to Complete Trade with Clippers After NBA Probe
articles.summary: Now that Kawhi Leonard has avoided suspension in the wake of the NBA's discipline following an independent investigation into rules violations involving the Los Angeles Clippers, the Toronto Raptors are ready to go through with the trade for the two-time NBA Finals MVP.
articles.body:
Now that Kawhi Leonard has avoided suspension in the wake of the NBA's discipline following an independent investigation into rules violations involving the Los Angeles Clippers, the Toronto Raptors are ready to go through with the trade for the two-time NBA Finals MVP.

Per NBA insider Marc Stein , the Raptors are "eager" to complete their trade with the Clippers for Leonard and they "firmly believe that the deal will happen as agreed upon and intended."

Despite Toronto's eagerness, Stein did note people around the NBA have started to "wonder aloud" if the Clippers are delaying an agreement "to spite" Leonard:

"Yet the delay has naturally led some league observers to wonder aloud whether the Clippers are holding off — or considering something even more drastic — to spite Leonard for so readily accepting the league's punishment rather than invoking his right to pursue an appeal. Any formal appeal within the NBA's auspices in such matters, remember, must be initiated by the player in question rather than the team according to league by-laws.

"Multiple sources briefed on the situation nonetheless insisted to The Stein Line this week that Clippers continue to maintain that uncertainty about how their front office will function with owner Steve Ballmer suspended for one year and president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank suspended for six months is the true cause of the holdup."

The Clippers' discipline includes forfeiting first-round draft picks every year from 2029 to '33; one year suspensions for governor Steve Ballmer and president of business operations Gillian Zucker; and a six-month suspension for president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank.

Leonard was fined $700,000, but he will not be suspended.

Per ESPN's Brian Windhorst (h/t RealGM.com ), the trade between the Raptors and Clippers is expected to go through as it was originally constructed with no amendments.

Stein and Fischer reported on Tuesday that one potential hold up is due to the Clippers still working through their new front office structure with Ballmer, Zucker and Frank suspended.

According to Windhorst , the "likely" scenario is general manager Trent Redden will be put in charge of the basketball operations in Los Angeles for the time being.

The trade, which was originally agreed to on June 30, will send Leonard to Toronto with Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, second-round picks in 2030 and 2033 and rights to a first-round pick swap in 2027 going back to the Clippers.

On July 9, the Raptors released a statement saying they planned to wait until the NBA completed its investigation before going through with the trade because they "would assume the risk of any potential outcome" impacting Leonard's status.

The next key date on the calendar for the Raptors is Sept. 29 when they are scheduled to open training camp.

articles.title: Jonathan Kuminga Calls Wolves Contract 'One of the Best Decisions I've Made' After Rejecting Lakers
articles.summary: While the saga dragged on for longer than he probably wanted, veteran forward Jonathan Kuminga is happy with how his free agency concluded this summer.
articles.body:
While the saga dragged on for longer than he probably wanted, veteran forward Jonathan Kuminga is happy with how his free agency concluded this summer.

"Just looking back, I think I would say it's one of the best decisions I've made, just looking at the roster, looking at the young group of guys they have and just seeing what they've done in the past," he told reporters Thursday during an introductory press conference.

Kuminga settled on a two-year, $12.4 million deal, though the second year is a player option.

According to ESPN's Anthony Slater and Shams Charania , the Los Angeles Lakers, Chicago Bulls and Portland Trail Blazers tabled formal offers to the 23-year-old. The Lakers specifically were prepared to give him "a similar starting role and $12 million-plus annually over three years."

Kuminga is setting himself up to potentially earn a bigger payday next summer, and he's nothing if not confident in his own abilities.

Minnesota is fifth in Bleacher Report's NBA power rankings after having added Kuminga and LaMelo Ball. The Wolves aren't championship favorites, but they should make a deep run. Any team success would boost's Kuminga's value to prospective suitors.

But we've already seen this strategy backfire once before.

The Golden State Warriors re-signed Kuminga, only to trade him in February when it became clear their relationship was untenable. The Atlanta Hawks then weren't convinced enough to pick up his $24.3 million option for 2026-27, putting him on course to take a pay cut.

Kuminga should get plenty of playing time in Minnesota after the trades of Julius Randle and Naz Reid thinned out the frontcourt. He figures to be the starting 4 alongside center Rudy Gobert and Jaden McDaniels.

But it's incumbent upon Kuminga to either make a major breakthrough — the kind that proved elusive in Golden State — or show he can excel in more of a supporting role. He's running out of time to prove he still has a level of untapped potential that failed to materialize during his first five years in the NBA.

articles.title: Jonathan Kuminga Hypes LaMelo Ball as Best Passer He's Played with Despite Curry, CP3 Pairings
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves forward Jonathan Kuminga teamed up with a couple legendary point guards in Stephen Curry and Chris Paul during his time with the Golden State Warriors, and he'll now play with another talented floor general in LaMelo Ball.
articles.body:

articles.title: Francia arrasa y Alemania da la sorpresa eliminando a Bélgica
articles.standfirst: Ambos equipos se medirán en la primera semifinal del Mundial este sábado
articles.summary: Ambos equipos se medirán en la primera semifinal del Mundial este sábado
articles.body: Francia y Alemania abrirán el fuego de las semifinales este próximo sábado a las 16.30. Ambos equipos sellaron sus billetes en los partidos que jugaron después del triunfo de Estados Unidos y justo antes de que saltara a la cancha la selección española. Las galas volvieron a arrasar y siguen dando miedo y las alemanas, tras perder por 30 en la jornada inaugural ante España, lucharán por medalla tras dejar fuera a Bélgica, vigente campeona de Europa. Francia no falló. Aniquiló a China como ha hecho con todos sus rivales. Las asiáticas aguantaron sólo hasta el primer cuarto, 20-25, y al descanso ya se dejaban 17 puntos ante un equipo que es un rodillo, 31-48. Entre Johannes (15), Salaun (15) y una formidable Gaby Williams (14+7), Francia acabó ganando de forma plácida, 61-90, tras dar 25 asistencias y meterse en las semifinales como el equipo más en forma del campeonato. Si les respeta el aspecto psicológico cuando algún partido vaya torcido, son más candidatas al oro que nadie. En el siguiente partido el Mundial recibió con los brazos abiertos en las semifinales al anfitrión. El Uber Arena estalló de alegría por el partido de las germanas que se cargaron a una de las favoritas, Bélgica, que no peleará por medalla. En un partido redondo Alemania ganó 74-93 y probablemente cerró la era dorada del baloncesto belga femenino. Las Messeman, Allemand, Vanloo o Massey no tienen recambios y se avecina una época más sombría para el equipo que ha dominado en los últimos Eurobasket. Alemania, sólida, ya llegó con ventaja al final del primer cuarto, 19-22 y al descanso había aumentado su ventaja, 35-42. Fue en un extraordinario tercer cuarto, 24-32, cuando cimentó su triunfo, que acabó siendo muy holgado, dando la gran campanada de este Mundial.
